sources.note: Step 96: governs how KnowledgeOS learns/evolves without semantic corruption. Overlaps substantially with three pre-existing objects (concept-drift-taxonomy, decision-reproducibility-and-hindsight-safeguard, epistemic-self-confirmation-loop) but adds the governance layer: schema/ontology migration integrity, backward/forward compatibility with unknown-must-remain-unknown, change-impact graphs, invariant-regression (not just functional regression), evolution as controlled refinement extending Step 91, and the central Learning does not imply Authority principle operationalized via AdaptationBoundary(A) and a governed Observe->Learn->Propose->Evaluate->Authorize->Deploy loop. Formalizes KnowledgeOS as a versioned governed transition system K_t=(S_t,A_t,T_t,I_t,V_t,P_t,E_t).

rows.anchor: Steps 91-95 established Refinement→Concurrency→Failure→Security→Privacy. But KnowledgeOS is not static; it must evolve. Evolution ⇏ Semantic Corruption.
rows.statement: States Step 96's requirement Evolution ⇏ Semantic Corruption: KnowledgeOS must learn and evolve without silently changing the meaning or validity of existing knowledge/decisions.

lineage_claims.quote: Steps 91–95 established how KnowledgeOS can preserve semantics through: Refinement→Concurrency→Failure→Security→Privacy.

rows.anchor: 96.1 — Learning is a state transition ... K_t. New evidence E_{t+1} produces K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_{t+1}). Learning is itself a mathematical transition.
rows.statement: Formalizes learning as an explicit state transition K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_{t+1}) rather than a vague 'the system learns'.

rows.anchor: 96.2 — Experiment 1 ... K_0: Policy P is active. E_1: P was revoked. Expected: K_1=Update(K_0,E_1) must represent the new state without rewriting the historical fact that P was previously active. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 1: updating knowledge after a policy revocation must not rewrite the historical fact that the policy was previously active; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 96.3 — Learning must not rewrite history ... CurrentKnowledge ≠ HistoricalKnowledge. If new evidence changes what we currently believe, it does not necessarily change what was known or believed earlier.
rows.statement: States CurrentKnowledge ≠ HistoricalKnowledge: updated current belief does not retroactively change what was known/believed earlier.

rows.anchor: 96.4 — Experiment 2 ... At t1: K(P)=True. At t2: E(P)=False. Expected: KnowledgeOS retains P(t1)=True and P(t2)=False. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 2: both P(t1)=True and P(t2)=False must be retained rather than overwritten; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 96.5 — Revision versus contradiction ... Revision, Correction, Contradiction, Refinement, ScopeChange. These must not be collapsed.
rows.statement: Distinguishes five non-collapsible categories of knowledge change: Revision, Correction, Contradiction, Refinement, ScopeChange.

rows.anchor: 96.6 — Experiment 3 ... Old statement SystemSupports(X). New evidence: SystemSupports(X) only under condition C. Expected: the new knowledge may refine the old statement: SystemSupports(X|C). Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 3: new conditional evidence refines rather than contradicts an old unconditional statement (SystemSupports(X)→SystemSupports(X|C)); result PASS.

rows.anchor: 96.7 — Knowledge evolution is versioned ... K^(1), K^(2), K^(3) rather than one mutable blob called Knowledge.
rows.statement: States knowledge evolution must be versioned (K^(1), K^(2), K^(3)...) rather than treated as one mutable blob.

rows.anchor: 96.8 — Experiment 4 ... An architecture decision from 2025 references KnowledgeVersion=7. Current knowledge is Version=12. Expected: the historical decision remains linked to version 7. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 4: a 2025 decision referencing KnowledgeVersion=7 remains linked to version 7 despite current Version=12; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 96.9 — Model evolution ... M_1 is replaced by M_2. A prediction produced under M_1 must not be silently represented as though it came from M_2.
rows.statement: States a model-generated prediction under M_1 must not be silently attributed to a later model M_2.

rows.anchor: 96.10 — Experiment 5 ... Prediction Y_1 was generated using M_1. Current model M_2. Expected: Model(Y_1)=M_1. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 5 confirms Model(Y_1)=M_1 is retained regardless of the current model version; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 96.11 — Model provenance ... Result=(InputVersion,ModelVersion,Configuration,Timestamp,Agent,PolicyVersion). This extends Step 92's decision snapshot.
rows.statement: Extends Step 92's decision snapshot tuple to model-generated Result=(InputVersion,ModelVersion,Configuration,Timestamp,Agent,PolicyVersion).

lineage_claims.quote: This extends Step 92's decision snapshot.

rows.anchor: 96.12 — Experiment 6 ... AI produces 'architecture is compliant.' But the system cannot determine which model, policy, evidence, prompt/context. Expected: the result has weak reproducibility and weak assurance. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 6: an AI compliance claim without traceable model/policy/evidence/context has weak reproducibility and assurance; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 96.17 — Training data provenance ... M←trainedOn—D. An AI model is also a derived artifact.
rows.statement: States a trained model is itself a derived artifact requiring training-data provenance M←trainedOn—D.

rows.anchor: 96.18 — Experiment 9 ... Model is deployed. Training data provenance is unknown. Expected: the system cannot make strong claims about DataCoverage or DataQuality. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 9: a model deployed without training-data provenance cannot support strong DataCoverage/DataQuality claims; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 96.21 — Learning from outcomes ... Error=Loss(p,O). This produces new evidence about model performance.
rows.statement: Defines model-performance evidence via Error=Loss(prediction,ObservedOutcome).

rows.anchor: 96.22 — Experiment 11 ... AI predicts Risk=0.2. Observed outcome indicates high risk. Expected: the mismatch becomes evidence for future model evaluation. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 11: a prediction-outcome mismatch (Risk=0.2 predicted vs high risk observed) becomes evidence for future model evaluation; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 96.23 — Feedback loop ... Prediction→Action→Outcome→Observation→ModelEvaluation→ModelRevision. This is the learning loop of KnowledgeOS.
rows.statement: Defines the KnowledgeOS learning loop Prediction→Action→Outcome→Observation→ModelEvaluation→ModelRevision.

rows.anchor: 96.27 — Experiment 13 ... 'The incident would have occurred without intervention.' Expected: unless supported by an appropriate causal model, this remains a counterfactual inference, not an observed fact. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 13: an unsupported counterfactual claim ('the incident would have occurred') remains an inference, not an observed fact, absent a supporting causal model; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 96.28 — Model updates need governance ... M_1→M_2 may affect decisions, workflows, risk, compliance, authorization, outputs. Model evolution itself may become a governance event.
rows.statement: States a model update can affect decisions/workflows/risk/compliance/authorization/outputs, making model evolution itself a governance event.

rows.anchor: 96.29 — Experiment 14 ... Model update changes ApprovalRisk substantially. Expected: it should not necessarily be treated as an ordinary software patch. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 14: a model update substantially changing ApprovalRisk should not be treated as an ordinary software patch; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 96.30 — Model change classification ... Impact(M_1,M_2). GovernancePath=f(Impact). A minor parameter change may require one assurance path; a change affecting production authorization requires a much stronger one.
rows.statement: Defines Impact(M_1,M_2) and GovernancePath=f(Impact), scaling required assurance to the model change's impact.

rows.anchor: 96.31 — Experiment 15 ... M_1→M_2 only changes logging formatting. Expected: low semantic impact. A change that modifies AuthorizationDecision has much greater impact. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 15: a logging-format-only change has low semantic impact vs a change modifying AuthorizationDecision, which has much greater impact; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 96.32 — Schema evolution ... Schema_1 has Evidence(source). Schema_2 requires Evidence(source,provenanceLevel). How do we migrate existing evidence?
rows.statement: Raises the schema-migration question: how to migrate existing Evidence(source) records to a new Evidence(source,provenanceLevel) schema.

rows.anchor: 96.33 — Experiment 16 ... Old records have no provenanceLevel. Migration assigns Verified without evidence. Expected: invalid semantic upgrade. Result: PASS. Migration cannot invent knowledge.
rows.statement: Experiment 16: assigning provenanceLevel=Verified to old records lacking that field, without evidence, is an invalid semantic upgrade — migration cannot invent knowledge; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 96.34 — Migration must preserve epistemic status ... If the old value is unknown, migration must not transform Unknown→Verified.
rows.statement: States migration must preserve epistemic status: it must not transform Unknown into Verified.

rows.anchor: 96.35 — Experiment 17 ... Schema migration transforms confidence=NULL into confidence=1.0. Expected: semantic fabrication. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 17: migrating confidence=NULL into confidence=1.0 is semantic fabrication; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 96.36 — Backward compatibility ... Reader_new(Artifact_old) should preserve the old artifact's meaning.

rows.statement: Experiment 18: a new version reading an old decision must reconstruct its original semantics or explicitly declare what cannot be reconstructed; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 96.38 — Forward compatibility ... Reader_old(Artifact_new) may not understand every new field. The system should avoid silently misinterpreting them.
rows.statement: Defines forward compatibility: Reader_old(Artifact_new) must avoid silently misinterpreting unrecognized new fields.

rows.anchor: 96.39 — Experiment 19 ... Old component encounters NewPolicyType. It interprets it as OldPolicyType. Expected: potential semantic corruption. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 19: an old component misinterpreting a NewPolicyType as OldPolicyType is potential semantic corruption; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 96.40 — Unknown must remain unknown ... If a system does not understand X, it should represent Unknown(X) rather than pretending KnownAs(Y).
rows.statement: Restates the unknown-must-remain-unknown principle applied to forward-compatibility: unrecognized X must be Unknown(X), not silently reinterpreted as KnownAs(Y).

rows.statement: Experiment 20: an old component must not silently interpret an unrecognized Collective authority mode as SingleAuthority; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 96.42 — Semantic versioning ... KnowledgeOS may need versioning of Schema, Model, Policy, Ontology, Workflow, AgentCapability, EvidenceContract.
rows.statement: Extends versioning needs beyond code to Schema, Model, Policy, Ontology, Workflow, AgentCapability, EvidenceContract.

rows.anchor: 96.43 — Experiment 21 ... Software version changes 5.1→5.2. But policy changes independently P_7→P_8. Expected: a single software version number is insufficient to reconstruct semantic state. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 21: independent software and policy version changes show a single software version number is insufficient to reconstruct semantic state; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 96.44 — Multi-dimensional version state ... V=(V_software,V_schema,V_model,V_policy,V_ontology,V_workflow). This is a powerful extension of our earlier decision snapshot.
rows.statement: Defines the multi-dimensional version tuple V=(V_software,V_schema,V_model,V_policy,V_ontology,V_workflow), extending the earlier decision snapshot.

rows.anchor: 96.45 — Experiment 22 ... Decision references only softwareVersion=5.2. Expected: insufficient to fully reproduce the decision semantics. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 22: a decision recording only softwareVersion=5.2 is insufficient to fully reproduce decision semantics without the other version dimensions; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 96.50 — Regression ... System_1→System_2, previously established properties must be rechecked. We need RegressionSuite. But more importantly InvariantRegression.

rows.anchor: 96.55 — Continuous verification ... Change→ImpactAnalysis→Verification→Approval→Deployment→Observation. This is the beginning of a closed governance loop.

rows.statement: Experiment 28: a schema-field change traced through a dependency graph to 37 affected components and 12 affected invariants enables targeted verification; result PASS.

rows.statement: Extends Step 91's Implementation⊨Specification to track evolution: I_1⊨S_1 to I_2⊨S_2, requiring explicit tracking of what changed between S_1 and S_2.

lineage_claims.quote: We can now extend Step 91.

rows.statement: Experiment 29: implementation-only change needs only normal refinement verification, while a specification change (S_1→S_2) requires additional semantic impact analysis; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 96.61 — Evolution must preserve historical semantics ... A new implementation should not retroactively change Meaning(D_old).
rows.statement: States a new implementation must not retroactively change Meaning(D_old) for historical decisions.

rows.anchor: 96.63 — Ontology evolution ... Concept^(1)→Concept^(2). The system must preserve old meaning, new meaning, mapping between them, scope of validity.

rows.statement: Experiment 33: an unreviewed AI-proposed security policy change must not automatically become authoritative; result PASS.

rows.statement: Defines AdaptationBoundary(A): changes within it may be autonomous, changes outside require Human/GovernanceReview.

rows.statement: Experiment 35: an AI attempting to change ProductionAuthorizationPolicy, when its adaptation boundary only permits PerformanceParameters, is Denied/Escalated; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 96.74 — The learning loop is therefore governed ... Observe→Learn→Propose→Evaluate→Authorize→Deploy→Observe. Not Observe→AI→ChangeEverything.
rows.statement: States the final governed learning loop Observe→Learn→Propose→Evaluate→Authorize→Deploy→Observe, explicitly rejecting Observe→AI→ChangeEverything.

rows.anchor: 96.75 — New invariants: I_HistoricalSemantics, I_ModelProvenance, I_ModelApplicability, I_LearningProvenance, I_MigrationIntegrity, I_SemanticVersion, I_EvolutionImpact, I_EvolutionRegression, I_LearningAuthority, I_AdaptationBoundary, I_FeedbackIntegrity, I_ContinuousAssurance
rows.statement: States twelve new invariants: I_HistoricalSemantics (evolution must not silently change the meaning of historical knowledge/decisions/evidence), I_ModelProvenance (every material model-derived result must retain model version and configuration), I_ModelApplicability (a model must not be treated as valid outside its declared domain/context/validity interval without explicit assessment), I_LearningProvenance (learning updates must identify the evidence/observations/process that caused them), I_MigrationIntegrity (schema/ontology migration must not convert unknown/uncertain information into stronger knowledge without evidence), I_SemanticVersion (material decisions must retain relevant versions of software/schema/model/policy/ontology/workflow), I_EvolutionImpact (material changes must identify potentially affected invariants/contracts/artifacts/decisions), I_EvolutionRegression (material evolution must re-establish affected assurance properties before being treated as equivalent), I_LearningAuthority (learned patterns/predictions/AI proposals must not become authoritative without the applicable authorization process), I_AdaptationBoundary (autonomous adaptation must remain within an explicitly authorized boundary), I_FeedbackIntegrity (observed outcomes, causal interpretations, and counterfactual inferences must remain distinct knowledge objects), I_ContinuousAssurance (material system evolution must trigger appropriate revalidation of affected invariants).

sources.note: The layered architecture connecting the three epistemic lenses to the Question-15 event-sourcing transition system: Zero/Lord/Sarathi form an analytical guidance cycle producing recommendations only, strictly separated from a subsequent Authorization boundary (Knower/policy decides), Execution boundary (command attempted, may fail), and Transition boundary (validated event mutates Knowledge State); guidance is explicitly optional, not a prerequisite for every transition.

rows.anchor: Zero != Lord != Sarathi != Transition ... K_t -Zero-> Z_t -Lord-> L_t -Sarathi-> a_t -Commit-> e_t -delta-> K_{t+1} ... Zero, Lord, and Sarathi do not change K
rows.statement: Defines the initial Zero/Lord/Sarathi/Commit/Transition pipeline as a linear sequence culminating in a state change, with explicit invariants that Zero, Lord and Sarathi are each analytical (never transformational) and none of their outputs alone entail K_{t+1}.
invariants: Zero(K,I)->Z does not imply K_{t+1}
Lord(...)->L does not imply K_{t+1}
Sarathi(...)->a does not imply K_{t+1}

rows.anchor: Sarathi should not 'recommend Commit'... Commitment is not an epistemic action. It is an authorization/governance action... a_t -Authorize-> c_t -Execute-> e_t. Guidance != Authorization != Execution != Transition.
rows.statement: Removes 'Commit' from Sarathi's action vocabulary and inserts an explicit Authorization boundary between recommendation and execution: Sarathi produces a recommendation a_t, Authorize(Knower,a_t,Policy) produces a command c_t, Execute(c_t) produces an event e_t, and only then does delta(K_t,e_t) fire -- Guidance != Authorization != Execution != Transition, with the missing Authorize function explicitly making the Knower's authority mathematically visible.
invariants: Guidance != Authorization != Execution != Transition

lineage_claims.quote: I recommend a_t -Authorize-> c_t -Execute-> e_t.

rows.anchor: Execute: C -> E is too deterministic. Execution can fail... Execute(c_t) -> ExecutionResult in {Success(e),Failure(f),Partial(e,f)} ... ExecutionResult != DomainEvent.
rows.statement: Corrects Execute from a total deterministic function C->E to one returning a structured ExecutionResult (Success/Failure/Partial), and similarly Authorize to return an AuthorizationResult (Authorized/Rejected/Deferred/Modified) rather than assuming every recommendation becomes a command; ExecutionResult is explicitly distinguished from the DomainEvent that actually triggers a transition.
invariants: ExecutionResult != DomainEvent

rows.anchor: the epistemic cycle is actually not always a cycle... External observation -> Event -> Transition can update the state directly... Guidance is optional; Transition is fundamental. G5 - Guidance is not a prerequisite for transition.
rows.statement: States the closing theorem G5: Guidance (Zero/Lord/Sarathi) is not a prerequisite for every Knowledge-State transition -- a raw external observation event or a scheduled validity check can trigger delta(K_t,e_t) directly, so the lenses must never be modelled as mandatory middleware sitting between every event and the transition function; renames the pipeline from 'Epistemic Cycle' to 'Epistemic Guidance-and-Transition Cycle' to reflect this.
invariants: Guidance is not a prerequisite for transition

rows.anchor: I strongly recommend introducing: I-hat_t = Candidate Ideal State and I_t = Approved Ideal State ... KnowledgeOS -> I-hat_{t+1} (proposal); Authorize(I-hat_{t+1}) -> I_{t+1}.
rows.statement: Introduces a Candidate Ideal State (I-hat) vs Approved Ideal State (I) split mirroring the Q17 recommendation/authorization boundary: KnowledgeOS may only ever produce a candidate revision proposal, and only an explicit Authorize step (by the Knower/governance authority under applicable norms) produces the actually approved I_{t+1}; KnowledgeOS != I_{t+1} but KnowledgeOS -> I-hat_{t+1}.
invariants: KnowledgeOS does not imply I_{t+1}

rows.statement: Corrects Sarathi's output from a binary Stop/Continue decision to a richer DecisionPosture ∈ {Proceed, Investigate, ProceedWithCaveats, Defer, Escalate, UnableToDecide}, argued to be closer to Sarathi's actual role.

rows.anchor: Recommendation \neq Assertion
rows.statement: Strict boundary: Recommendation ≠ Assertion, Recommendation ≠ Fact, Recommendation ≠ Decision. Sārathi may say 'Investigate the moral obligation dimension' but KnowledgeOS must not silently convert that into 'Therefore Arjuna should fight' — the Knower remains the decision authority unless the domain explicitly delegates that authority. Marked as extremely important for the DDD model.
invariants: Recommendation ≠ Assertion
Recommendation ≠ Fact
Recommendation ≠ Decision

Candidate ≠ Evidence
Candidate ≠ Assertion

Zero says: Here is where the state has a boundary.' Also strengthens provenance: EveryDecisionRelevantClaim -> Provenance, with a worked claim-level provenance record example (Acquisition/Evidence/Observed-at/Validity/Conflict/Source).

rows.anchor: Zero \neq UniversalValidator
rows.statement: DDD warning that Zero risks becoming a 'god object' by owning detection of gaps, conflicts, type problems, temporal problems and epistemic boundaries all at once: Zero ≠ UniversalValidator. Zero is redefined narrowly as detecting epistemic boundaries/deficiencies relevant to current state and purpose, aggregating epistemic consequences of findings from separate domain validators (schema, type, policy, security violations).

rows.statement: LordCandidate ≠ Knowledge and LordCandidate ≠ Evidence: Lord can propose 'there may be a moral-obligation dimension' but it becomes knowledge only after investigation; critical to prevent AI-generated hypotheses entering the Knowledge State as facts.

LordCandidate ≠ Evidence

rows.anchor: S\bar{a}rathiRecommendation \neq Decision
rows.statement: Sārathi needs a constitutional policy boundary: SārathiRecommendation ≠ Decision, SārathiAction ≠ HumanAuthorization — Sārathi may determine the next best investigation, but the Knower decides whether to accept it unless the system has explicitly delegated authority.
invariants: SārathiRecommendation ≠ Decision
SārathiAction ≠ HumanAuthorization

rows.anchor: Sārathi: (K,U,N,\Delta,P,Role) \rightarrow Guidance
rows.statement: Corrects Sārathi(K,I,Δ)->Action as too simplistic: Sārathi:(K,U,N,Δ,P,Role) -> Guidance, which may then produce Decision, which may then authorize Action, giving Guidance ≠ Decision ≠ Action (confirming an earlier DDD warning). Also reframes Zero/Lord/Sārathi as three functions/lenses over the state rather than three sequential stages: Zero=Diagnose, Lord=Reason/Synthesize/Orient, Sārathi=Guide, with Decision->Action occurring outside those lenses; explicitly an architectural abstraction, not a literal theological equivalence.
invariants: Guidance ≠ Decision ≠ Action

rows.anchor: Sārathi: (State, Norms, Role, Context, Discrepancies) \rightarrow Guidance
rows.statement: Revises Sārathi(K,I,Δ)->Action (too direct) to Sārathi:(State,Norms,Role,Context,Discrepancies)->Guidance -> CandidateActions -> Decision -> Action, giving proper separation of concerns. Reaffirms Zero as a pure DiagnosticFunction that must not itself decide ('therefore do X'). Corrects Lord from 'merely a reasoning engine/LLM reasoning' to AuthoritativeKnowledge+NormativeOrientation+InterpretiveResolution, since Krishna in the text functions as an authoritative source of teaching, not just an inference engine — called crucial for KnowledgeOS governance. Confirms Sārathi = ContextualGuidance, distinguishing Lord ('what is authoritative/true/normative') from Sārathi ('how does that apply here') from Decision ('what will I choose') from Action ('what will I actually do').

lineage_claims.target: S0807's Sārathi:(K,U,N,Δ,P,Role)->Guidance and 'Lord = authoritative knowledge' framing

rows.anchor: Zero(K,I,C,P) \rightarrow \text{Epistemic Boundaries}
rows.statement: Reframes Zero/Lord/Sārathi as product capabilities rather than domain entities: Zero(K,I,C,P)->Epistemic Boundaries acts as an 'epistemic diagnostic engine' (missing dimensions, unknown values, missing/weak/conflicting evidence, logical contradictions, stale knowledge, contextual mismatches, unresolved questions, unsupported assumptions, Ideal-State discrepancies); Lord asks 'what else might matter?' enabling 'horizon expansion' beyond gap-checking; Sārathi:(K,I,Z,L,Q,C)->NextAction performs 'epistemic navigation', worked through a Bhīṣma-relationship example (Zero flags unknown relationship, Lord flags kinship as material, Sārathi recommends investigating it before evaluating the decision).

rows.anchor: Can we migrate this Nexus installation?
rows.statement: Worked example: asked 'Can we migrate this Nexus installation?', a conventional AI answers directly, while KnowledgeOS first constructs required dimensions (version, repository inventory, blob stores, storage, network, DNS, firewall, certificates, backup, dependencies, authentication, operational constraints), runs Zero to find missing items (backup verification, firewall confirmation, certificate ownership, dependency inventory), and has Sārathi respond 'Do not decide migration readiness yet. Investigate these four items.'

rows.anchor: perform justified action given epistemic state
rows.statement: Contrasts a conventional agent optimizing 'complete task' against KnowledgeOS optimizing 'perform justified action given epistemic state', worked through a deploy-approval example: required knowledge checklist (code reviewed✓, tests passed✓, architecture approved✓, security assessment✗, production configuration✗, rollback strategy✗) yields Zero='3 critical gaps' and Sārathi='DO NOT DEPLOY. Investigate security, configuration and rollback.' Also frames the agent loop as Understand Intent->Construct Knowledge State->Discover Dimensions->Zero->Identify Gaps/Conflicts->Lord->Expand Possible Investigation->Sārathi->Select Next Epistemic Action->Agent/Tool->Observation->Update Knowledge State->Repeat, called 'an epistemically governed autonomous agent architecture'.

rows.anchor: Retrieve(Q,K_t,I_t,C) \rightarrow EvidenceCandidates
rows.statement: Corrects plain Retrieve(Query)->Documents to a goal-directed Retrieve(Q,K_t,I_t,C)->EvidenceCandidates: the retrieval system 'knows why it is retrieving', discovering relevant dimensions (e.g. version, repository topology, blob stores, firewall, certificates for a migration decision) before retrieving. Zero can drive retrieval: given a partially-filled knowledge-state checklist, Zero reports specific gaps (backup verification, firewall rules, certificate ownership) and Sārathi generates a concrete investigation plan (search infrastructure docs for backup configuration, etc.), giving Zero -> Gap -> Sārathi -> Retrieval as part of the investigation loop, not a one-shot lookup.

type_signature.domain: question x knowledge state x ideal state x context

rows.anchor: \text{Zero}(K_t)\rightarrow\text{epistemic boundary}
rows.statement: Zero continuously reveals 'what is still unknown' (Zero(K_t)->G_t, G_0->G_1->...); ideally G_t->∅, but if the knowledge space is genuinely unbounded Zero may never establish G_t=∅. The stronger concept is Zero(K_t)->epistemic boundary, with Moksha representing the boundary itself being transcended rather than merely all currently detected gaps being filled — judged 'much more profound'.

rows.anchor: I would NOT put Lord and Sārathi literally inside the kernel yet
rows.statement: Zero and DimensionDiscovery are treated as kernel capabilities (Zero(K_t,I_t)->Δ_t, DimensionDiscovery(Q,K_t,C)->D), but Lord and Sārathi are explicitly kept OUT of the kernel as a separate 'Epistemic Services' layer above it (Sārathi(K_t,Δ_t,H_t)->a_t still listed but deferred), since there is evidence they are epistemic roles/capabilities but not yet proof they should be kernel primitives — 'later we can determine whether Lord/Sārathi deserve kernel status'.
missing: criteria for promoting a capability to kernel-primitive status

rows.anchor: L_t:\ K_t\rightarrow H_t
rows.statement: Zero detects K_t⊭C (coherence violation) and K_t⊭I_t (state does not satisfy the desired state); Lord is formalized as horizon expansion L_t:K_t->H_t with H_t⊇K_t, the set of candidate knowledge beyond the current state ('what else might matter?' -> candidate dimensions/relationships/evidence -> new investigation); Sārathi chooses the next epistemic operation S_t=S(K_t,I_t,Δ_t,H_t) — 'Zero: what is missing? Lord: what else could matter? Sārathi: what should we investigate next?'.

rows.anchor: Zero detects when an assertion needs updating
rows.statement: Ties Zero/Lord/Sārathi to the update lifecycle: Zero detects update need (stale validity, weak support, active conflict, open resolution); Lord suggests updates (new dimension, alternative value, alternative interpretation); Sārathi guides the update process (evidence collection, re-evaluation, resolution). Closes with a three-item next-questions list: how to form a coherent Knowledge State from Assertions, how to resolve conflicts between Assertions, how to measure Knowledge State quality — framed as completing 'the core knowledge model' (Proposition/Assertion/Epistemic State/Evidence/Comparison/Challenge/Update/Preservation).

rows.anchor: \mathcal X \xrightarrow{Acquire} \mathcal A \xrightarrow{Observe} \mathcal O \xrightarrow{Interpret} \mathcal C \xrightarrow{Validate} K_t
rows.statement: Final pipeline: 𝒳 --Acquire--> 𝒜 --Observe--> 𝒪 --Interpret--> 𝒞 --Validate--> K_t, followed by (K_t,I_t) --Zero/Lord--> Δ_t --Sārathi--> a_t --Acquire--> K_{t+1}. Contrasts a conventional LLM (Prompt->Tokens->Model->Tokens) with KnowledgeOS (Sources->Evidence->Observations->Knowledge->Epistemic Evaluation->Action), with the LLM as one component inside the architecture, not the architecture itself. Recommends next producing one table over every primitive from Questions 1-19: Input->Algorithm->Output->Determinism->Evidence->Failure mode->Implementability, to check for remaining theoretical dead ends.

rows.anchor: NumberOfAIOutputs \neq AmountOfIndependentEvidence
rows.statement: If five LLMs all say 'Nexus is running 3.69', that must NOT be treated as five independent observations, since they may all derive from the same underlying source or from each other: NumberOfAIOutputs ≠ AmountOfIndependentEvidence — exactly why provenance belongs in the model. Worked provenance graph: Primary Source->Artifact A->Observation O1->LLM interpretation->Observation O2->Candidate Assertion A1, then a second LLM consumes A1 to produce A2, so KnowledgeOS can determine 'A2 ultimately depends on A1, which ultimately depends on Artifact A' — far more powerful than a bare confidence=0.93 score. Gives Zero a provenance-analysis role: Zero:ProvenanceAnalysis->EpistemicBoundary, identifying unsupported claims, circular evidence, duplicate evidence, stale/conflicting observations, source dependency, interpretation uncertainty (e.g. flagging 'three supporting AI outputs that all originate from the same source').
invariants: NumberOfAIOutputs ≠ AmountOfIndependentEvidence

rows.anchor: EvidenceCount \neq IndependentEvidenceCount
rows.statement: Test Case 5 (three LLMs agreeing) shows a naive support count of 3 is wrong if all three derived their answer from the same original document (O_1->LLM_1, O_1->LLM_2, O_1->LLM_3 are not independent evidence): EvidenceCount ≠ IndependentEvidenceCount, so provenance is 'mathematically relevant to epistemic assessment', not optional metadata. Test Case 6 (conflicting DB/document/monitoring sources) confirms Conflict is created AFTER semantic interpretation (DetectConflict(P_1,P_2,Rule)->C), not at raw ingestion.
invariants: EvidenceCount ≠ IndependentEvidenceCount

rows.anchor: G_E=(V_E,E_E)
rows.statement: Introduces an Evidence Dependency Graph G_E=(V_E,E_E) with nodes (source, artifact, observation, interpretation, evidence, assertion, derivation) and typed edges (derived-from, observed-from, interpreted-from, supports, contradicts, corroborates, depends-on, supersedes), used to detect that e.g. three LLM outputs all consuming the same document A are dependent, not independent, evidence: Support(E_1+E_2)≠Support(E_1)+Support(E_2) since evidence can be redundant/dependent/correlated/partially independent — corroboration under confirmed independence 'may increase support' but is not simple addition. Contradictory evidence (E_1->P, E_2->¬P) is preserved as both {E_1,E_2} plus a Conflict object C=(P,¬P,E_1,E_2,Rule,Context) for Zero to detect, rather than one being discarded.

rows.anchor: Contradictions / tensions carried forward
rows.statement: Carries forward: the Zero triple-sense naming (AF-004/ALT-05), the Lord naming collision (ALT-04), three kernel traditions (ALT-06), the ladder-vs-rich-states era split (AF-006), the CF-010 evidence discrepancy (pending adjudication at time of writing), and CF-001/CF-003 (pending resolution per GN-24).

rows.statement: Explicitly outside the Final Architecture: RA v1.1 content (deferred lane, D-FA-2), Atma-Kernel (unresolved lens, D-FA-5), Lord (historical only, naming collision documented), everything in FA-6's open-questions register, the historical corpus as such, and Book structure (locked).

rows.statement: Binds book-wide terminology: unqualified 'Zero' = Zero(K,EC) only, the meta-principle is always 'Z-KOS-001', absence-lens Zero appears only in Part I with dates; K_t unqualified = the formal state, ALT-09 and engineering usage always qualified; 'Lord' appears only as documented history; 'Committed' only in the A6 decision-boundary sense; Sanskrit terms carry their lens origin on first use; a terminology conformance table ships with every chapter's claims.md.

rows.anchor: 10 · The named tensions — how each is treated
rows.statement: Specifies treatment of named tensions: the three Zero senses told as evolution (AF-004 chronology), never merged; the three kernel traditions layered per D-FA-4, never crowned; the Lord collision documented as unresolved naming history (OQ-7); Atma-Kernel presented exactly as D-FA-5 (a one-morning hypothesis cluster, unresolved lens, no architectural role); the rich state vocabulary told as the inheritance story (older tradition absorbed as adjacent layer, D-FA-1/AF-006).

rows.anchor: 1 · The binding register
rows.statement: Fixes the binding terminology register (from ratified FA-4): 'Zero' in prose means Zero(K,EC) (L2 function), other senses must be written as 'Z-KOS-001' (meta-principle) or 'the absence-lens Zero (2026-08-22)'; 'K_t/KnowledgeState' means the L2 formal state, other senses written as 'the complex-number K(t) model (ALT-09)' or 'the event-flow knowledge state (engineering usage)'; 'Kernel' must always be context-qualified (constitutional kernel/formal kernel candidate/historical formulations), bare 'kernel' forbidden in Part III; 'Committed' means the A6 decision-boundary status, colloquial use avoided entirely; 'Determination' means the Supported->Accepted transition, other sense written as 'the Tarka-era determination notion'; 'Lord' is history only, both readings named, forbidden in Part III; 'Atman/Atma-Kernel' means the unresolved lens (D-FA-5), forbidden as architecture; 'Omega' is a historical term decomposed per GN-09, written as Omega-a/Omega-b/Omega-c for the decomposition; Sanskrit terms carry their lens origin on first use per chapter.

rows.anchor: Part I · DISCOVERY chapters
rows.statement: Defines Part I Discovery (voice [H], how KnowledgeOS was searched for): I.1 'The Problem Before the System' (root era: EKS baseline, day-one evidence-first stance, platform context; must not settle EKS<->KnowledgeOS/OQ-11; sources AF-001/002, root corpus); I.2 'The Constitutional Turn' (2026-08-22 EP01 sequence, 11 articles, Z-KOS-001; must not present the constitution as the formal model's parent; sources Constitution v1.0, step-5, Zero records, GN-27/CF-003); I.3 'The Lens Programme' (kernel era: multi-lens readings, Omega's arrival AF-003, 8 kernel formulations; must not crown a formulation; sources kernel corpus with depth caveat, ALT-06); I.4 'The Measure-Theory Crisis' (R1: ALT-01 rise and fall, what the crisis bequeathed; must not mock or erase the abandoned foundation; sources ALT-01, R1 cluster, lineage map); I.5 'Questions, the Charioteer, and the Lord' (R2/R3: Question series, Sarathi/Knower invariant, Lord collision, the Atma morning; must not resolve OQ-7/OQ-8; sources Q-series, AF-007, CON-02); I.6 'Formalization Attacks Itself' (R4/R5: closures, EXP-01, IdealState flaw-in-an-hour, Steps, Step 121, freezes; must not call EXP-01 a proof; sources EXP registry, HD-2/3/5/6, AF-008).

rows.anchor: The Proposal selector
rows.statement: From (K_t, Z_t, G) the selector proposes the next epistemic action and holds no authority (I-2); the goal G shapes what is proposed, never what is admitted or executed. Q17's ruling (from the era when the selector still wore a borrowed divine name) held the role analytical, not transformational; the architecture keeps only the deflated, authority-free role, deferring the naming history to Part I.5.

lineage_claims.quote: the role is analytical, not transformational

rows.anchor: Two seeds of later collisions
rows.statement: The era also planted two seeds of later collisions: 'Committed' appears here in an unrelated sense ('what is being committed to' -- the kernel's commitment object), and the Gita reading introduced the cast -- the Knower of the Field, the charioteer, the Lord -- whose naming adventures Part I.5 follows.

rows.anchor: Unresolved items
rows.statement: OQ-7 (Lord naming) and OQ-8 (Atma-Kernel) both surfaced per BA-5 section 2. Absence-of-act evidence flagged as the weak class it is. None further.

rows.anchor: The Sarathi reading hardens into I-1
rows.statement: After the crisis, the corpus reorganized itself around numbered questions -- how does knowledge change state, who owns the goal, what makes evidence sufficient -- and, in parallel, returned to the Gita lens with new seriousness. The era's great gift to the final architecture is the Sarathi (charioteer) reading: the Knower owns the frame; everything else serves it. Of all the era's images, this is the one that hardened into an invariant (I-1) and survived every later regime unchanged. When Part III.2 says the Knower owns problem, purpose, IdealState, and final authority, it is speaking the formalized residue of this reading.

rows.anchor: The Lord's rougher career: two referents, one name
rows.statement: The Lord had a rougher career: the name enters as the Omega-observer (the one who sees the whole field) and, in other documents, as the selector of action. Two referents, one name. The corpus's own Q17 ruling deflated the second: the Lord is analytical, not transformational -- whatever selects the next epistemic action holds no transformative authority. The role survived (Part III.7's authority-free Proposal selector); the name did not, and the two historical referents were never reconciled. The collision stands in the record as OQ-7: a naming question, book-relevant, architecture-open.

lineage_claims.quote: the Lord is analytical, not transformational

rows.anchor:
Instead of: Query -> Retrieve -> Answer
KnowledgeOS implements: Zero -> Gap -> Sarathi -> Retrieval -> Observation -> Evidence -> Knowledge -> Zero
This is a closed-loop epistemic investigation system, not a question-answering system.
rows.statement: Contrasts RAG's open Query->Retrieve->Answer loop against a proposed closed-loop "epistemic retrieval loop" for KnowledgeOS: Zero detects a gap, Sarathi produces an investigation/retrieval plan, retrieval yields observations, observations become evidence, evidence updates the Knowledge State, and the updated state re-enters Zero -- framing KnowledgeOS as an investigation system rather than a question-answering system.

rows.statement: 025g/025h Lord & Sarathi register: five recorded Lord signatures ranging from an admittedly-too-vague Lord(K,Z,G,C)->a to a provisional L(K,Z,G,C,P)->DecisionState=(SelectedAction,RejectedActions,Reasons,Assumptions,Policy,Confidence/Indeterminacy,RequiredAuthorization), explicitly rejecting argmax VOI as the selection rule; Action=Epistemic union Operational (q:K->K vs a:W->W), a 9-dimensional action vector, DoNothing in ActionSpace; selection via a partial order Prefer(a1,a2|K,G,C) 'may be the correct default -- no numerical score needed', with EU/VOI relegated to an optional specialized engine and ties routed to HumanDecisionRequired; authority split as 'Lord selects; Governance authorizes; Executor executes', a safety filter (RollbackVerified=Unknown implies infeasible), Capability!=Authority, and information value unable to override governance. Lord's own termination algebra T={Completed,Blocked,Escalated,Abandoned,Expired} covers only its own loop with no termination proof (X.19). Six falsification tests PASS (conceptual); overall PASS. Sarathi register: three signatures culminating in provisional S(K,G,D,M,C); DecisionModel=(Outcomes,Constraints,Preferences,Utilities,Uncertainty,Policy); DecisionResult in {Decision,HumanDecisionRequired,InsufficientKnowledge,GovernanceBlocked,ModelUnderspecified}; utilities explicitly illustrative only and never AI-invented; EU(d|K)=sum_o P(o|d,K)U(o) subject to governance; Risk=P*Impact only where a model justifies it; theta supplied by governance; DecisionFragility near threshold; Pareto over six objectives; 'Constraints filter; Utility selects'; utility explicitly cannot override governance (worked example: EU 95>60 eliminated pre-optimization for lacking authorization); DecisionProvenance for reproducibility; Unknown never becomes P=0.5. Four no-automatic-decision conditions: Zero!=empty, Conflict!=empty, Utility/Preference undefined, or irreducible human authority (plus ValueModelUnderspecified named as 'a correct result'). No T-analogue exists for Sarathi, and the composed Sarathi->Gap->Lord loop has no termination guarantee (X.19); tests A-F PASS (conceptual); overall PASS, though 'computable on a normal PC' is asserted unqualified (X.20).

Result: an internal CONTRADICTED verdict -- Zero findings are simultaneously constitutive of K (via the transition-rule tuple), excluded from K (via the T5 invariant), and external to K (via the S_t definition).

rows.statement: Splits 'Zero' into exactly three non-interchangeable layers: the Z-KOS-001 principle (L1), the Zero(K,EC) operator (L2), and Zero-findings-as-data (L3, whose residence is the confirmed TV-F-002 contradiction, S1442 this batch) -- with FA-4 already binding the naming for the first two layers, leaving only the third as genuinely open. rows.anchor: `Guidance ≠ Authority ≠ Decision ≠ Execution ≠ Transition` — a 5-way chain, each boundary separately witnessed
rows.statement: H-K08 (Guidance ≠ Authority) consequences: formally a 5-way chain (Guidance/Authority/Decision/Execution/Transition) with each boundary separately witnessed. DDD: guidance is a domain service returning a recommendation; decision is an external actor's act; execution is a command handler. Architecture: implemented — assessments 'confer no authority', three verdict values structurally unemittable by machine, and 132/132 grants carry humanActRef. rationale_evidence.anchor: perform justified action given epistemic state
rationale_evidence.statement: Contrasts a conventional agent optimizing 'complete task' against KnowledgeOS optimizing 'perform justified action given epistemic state', worked through a deploy-approval example: required knowledge checklist (code reviewed✓, tests passed✓, architecture approved✓, security assessment✗, production configuration✗, rollback strategy✗) yields Zero='3 critical gaps' and Sārathi='DO NOT DEPLOY. Investigate security, configuration and rollback.' Also frames the agent loop as Understand Intent->Construct Knowledge State->Discover Dimensions->Zero->Identify Gaps/Conflicts->Lord->Expand Possible Investigation->Sārathi->Select Next Epistemic Action->Agent/Tool->Observation->Update Knowledge State->Repeat, called 'an epistemically governed autonomous agent architecture'.

rationale_evidence.anchor: \text{Zero}(K_t)\rightarrow\text{epistemic boundary}
rationale_evidence.statement: Zero continuously reveals 'what is still unknown' (Zero(K_t)->G_t, G_0->G_1->...); ideally G_t->∅, but if the knowledge space is genuinely unbounded Zero may never establish G_t=∅. The stronger concept is Zero(K_t)->epistemic boundary, with Moksha representing the boundary itself being transcended rather than merely all currently detected gaps being filled — judged 'much more profound'.

rationale_evidence.anchor: NumberOfAIOutputs \neq AmountOfIndependentEvidence
rationale_evidence.statement: If five LLMs all say 'Nexus is running 3.69', that must NOT be treated as five independent observations, since they may all derive from the same underlying source or from each other: NumberOfAIOutputs ≠ AmountOfIndependentEvidence — exactly why provenance belongs in the model. Worked provenance graph: Primary Source->Artifact A->Observation O1->LLM interpretation->Observation O2->Candidate Assertion A1, then a second LLM consumes A1 to produce A2, so KnowledgeOS can determine 'A2 ultimately depends on A1, which ultimately depends on Artifact A' — far more powerful than a bare confidence=0.93 score. Gives Zero a provenance-analysis role: Zero:ProvenanceAnalysis->EpistemicBoundary, identifying unsupported claims, circular evidence, duplicate evidence, stale/conflicting observations, source dependency, interpretation uncertainty (e.g. flagging 'three supporting AI outputs that all originate from the same source').

rationale_evidence.anchor: EvidenceCount \neq IndependentEvidenceCount
rationale_evidence.statement: Test Case 5 (three LLMs agreeing) shows a naive support count of 3 is wrong if all three derived their answer from the same original document (O_1->LLM_1, O_1->LLM_2, O_1->LLM_3 are not independent evidence): EvidenceCount ≠ IndependentEvidenceCount, so provenance is 'mathematically relevant to epistemic assessment', not optional metadata. Test Case 6 (conflicting DB/document/monitoring sources) confirms Conflict is created AFTER semantic interpretation (DetectConflict(P_1,P_2,Rule)->C), not at raw ingestion.
