sources.note: Step 64's model-risk and self-validation layer: the world/parameter/model uncertainty trichotomy, ModelRisk distinct from PredictionError, Executable≠Validated, self-certification/circular-validation rejection with a model dependency graph, assumption-provenance impact propagation (Affected≠Invalid, evidence resilience), the adversarial-evidence Valid→Disputed→Invalidated lifecycle, model lineage/reproducibility (exact vs statistical replay), the two-dimensional OperationalHealth≠EpistemicValidity status, Model-performance≠Model-authorization, and governed self-healing. Extends champion-challenger-model-promotion-lifecycle (Step 45) and epistemic-anchor-redundancy-model (Step 47) into a full temporal-validity/drift/governance framework.

rows.anchor: World/parameter/model uncertainty trichotomy; ModelRisk(M,D,E) distinct from PredictionError
rows.statement: Separates World uncertainty (X~P(X), intrinsic variability), Parameter uncertainty (theta~P(theta|D), model structure accepted but parameters uncertain), and Model uncertainty (M in {M1,M2,...}, uncertain whether the model structure itself is appropriate) as fundamentally different -- Uncertainty != one single mathematical quantity. Worked example: P(Failure)=0.1 could mean intrinsically unpredictable failures (Case A), poorly estimated parameters (Case B), or a model that no longer describes the environment (Case C, 'particularly dangerous'). Defines ModelRisk(M,D,E) as the risk that a model's assumptions/behavior are unsuitable for the current environment, explicitly not simply PredictionError -- 'a model can temporarily make correct predictions while still being structurally inappropriate'.

rows.anchor: Parameter drift, distribution/covariate shift (DistributionShift⇏ModelFailure), concept drift, calibration decay with a model-status lifecycle (experiments 1-4)
rows.statement: Experiment 1: P_t0(Y|X) != P_t1(Y|X) detected as parameter drift needing possible recalibration, given tracked temporal model performance -- PASS. Experiment 2: P_train(X) != P_prod(X) detected as DistributionShiftDetected -- PASS; but explicitly DistributionShift ⇏ ModelFailure since P(Y|X) may remain unchanged -- 'a warning condition', not automatic failure. Experiment 3: P_t(Y=1|X=1) changing from 0.8 to 0.4 while the model keeps using the old relationship is detected as ConceptDrift -- PASS. Experiment 4: calibration monitored by temporal window; predictions remaining P=0.8 while realized success drops from ~80% to 55% is CalibrationDecay, and performance deteriorating beyond tolerance sets ModelStatus=Degraded -- PASS. Suggests a model lifecycle Experimental -> Validated -> Production -> Degraded -> Suspended -> Retired as domain/governance states, not mathematical truths.

lineage_claims.quote: More dangerous is: concept drift.

rows.anchor: Temporal (not permanent) model validation; Executable != Validated
rows.statement: States a model validated in 2025 is not automatically validated forever, so Validation(M,t) is more precise than Validation(M). Experiment 5: a model's validation validity period expires while it remains technically executable, giving ValidatedNow=False -- PASS. States the important architectural property Executable != Validated: 'a model may run successfully while no longer being trustworthy'.
invariants: Executable ≠ Validated

rows.anchor: Self-certification rejected as circular validation; DifferentModel⇏IndependentEvidence; model dependency graph G_M
rows.statement: Identifies the self-validation problem: Model_A evaluating Model_A with the same assumptions/outputs creates circular validation (A->A). Experiment 6: an AI asserting its own prediction is reliable with no independent outcome yields NotValidated -- PASS. Prefers Prediction -> ExternalOutcome -> Evaluation (evaluator: separate model, deterministic rules, measured outcome, human assessment, or independent statistical process). Warns two models trained on the same data sharing the same failure mechanism are not necessarily independent validators: DifferentModel ⇏ IndependentEvidence. Experiment 7: Model_B evaluating Model_A using the same generated predictions without independent outcomes yields validation strength not equivalent to independent validation -- PASS. Extends the provenance graph to a model dependency graph G_M=(Models,Dependencies) (M_A -> M_B if M_B's evaluation depends on M_A's outputs), preventing false claims of independent validation.
invariants: DifferentModel ⇏ IndependentEvidence: sharing training data/failure mechanisms defeats independent-validation claims

lineage_claims.target: epistemic-anchor-redundancy-model's common-mode epistemic failure and no-self-certification principles (Step 47)
lineage_claims.quote: But different model is not automatically independent.

rows.anchor: Assumption monitoring as first-class objects; assumption-evidence provenance chain enables impact propagation; Affected != Invalid; evidence resilience
rows.statement: Requires model assumptions A1,...,An (e.g. 'population is stable') to be represented as first-class objects; experiment 8: a violated assumption (A1: True -> False established by new evidence) triggers ModelValidity -> ReviewRequired -- PASS. Chains Model -> Assumption -> Evidence so invalidated evidence can be traced to affected models; via a dependency relation leadsto, defines Impact(x) = {y : x leadsto y} (impact/reachability analysis over claims, models, decisions, actions). Experiment 9: invalidating E1 and traversing the dependency graph correctly marks affected artifacts ReviewRequired -- PASS. Crucially, Affected != Invalid: experiment 10 shows a decision depending on E1,E2 remains DecisionValid=True after invalidating E1 if E2 alone suffices under policy -- PASS, motivating a domain-specific EvidenceResilience(D) metric (a decision is more resilient when it survives reasonable loss of individual evidence sources).
invariants: Affected ≠ Invalid: a dependency-graph-flagged artifact requires domain-specific reassessment, not automatic invalidation

rows.anchor: Adversarial evidence handling; rejecting an evidence item != deleting it; Valid->Disputed->Invalidated status lifecycle
rows.statement: Experiment 11: injecting evidence designed to drive P(p)->0.99 that contradicts known structural constraints yields EvidenceAnomaly, with the evidence preserved but not automatically promoted -- PASS. States the important principle: rejecting an evidence item != deleting the evidence -- the item remains part of the historical record with status Disputed or Invalidated, giving an explicit lifecycle Valid -> Disputed -> Invalidated with historical transitions remaining visible (never a silent 'delete evidence').
invariants: rejecting an evidence item never deletes it; it moves through a visible Valid→Disputed→Invalidated status history

rows.anchor: Model poisoning and lineage tracking; undocumented model change as a governance violation; SameModelVersion⇒SemanticallySameModel
rows.statement: Experiment 12: malicious/erroneous training data causing later performance degradation should let KnowledgeOS connect ModelDegradation to TrainingDataVersion, provided training provenance is preserved -- PASS, requiring lineage TrainingData -> TrainingRun -> ModelVersion -> Prediction -> Decision. A model version should ideally reference DataVersion, CodeVersion, Configuration, Dependencies, TrainingProcedure even where exact reproduction is infeasible. Experiment 13: model behavior changes with no corresponding version change, making historical decisions ambiguous -- GovernanceViolation -- PASS, giving the governance requirement SameModelVersion ⇒ SemanticallySameModel when reproducibility is claimed -- not necessarily byte-identical artifacts (hardware/library/floating-point/nondeterminism differences allowed), so 'same model' needs domain-specific reproducibility semantics.
invariants: SameModelVersion ⇒ SemanticallySameModel, whenever reproducibility is claimed

rows.anchor: Deterministic vs stochastic replay; ExactReplay vs StatisticalReplay (experiment 14)
rows.statement: Distinguishes deterministic computation f(x)=y from stochastic f(x,omega)=y (omega=randomness), the latter requiring a Seed(omega) for reproduction. Experiment 14: running a model twice with the same input and seed should give Output_1=Output_2 where algorithm/environment permits -- PASS. Notes exact determinism is not always required or meaningful: distinguishes ExactReplay from StatisticalReplay, where a stochastic simulation may only guarantee DistributionalConsistency (Y_1,...,Y_n ~ P_M(Y|X)) rather than Y_i=Y_i'.

rows.anchor: Six-field model monitoring vector MStatus(t); no universal scalar model-health score
rows.statement: Defines MStatus(t) = (Calibration, Accuracy, Drift, AssumptionValidity, DataQuality, OperationalHealth) -- 'no universal scalar model health score is required'.

lineage_claims.quote: No universal scalar model health score is required.

rows.anchor: OperationalHealth != EpistemicValidity; 'HTTP 200 does not mean ModelCorrect' (experiment 15, two-dimensional status)
rows.statement: States a model can be operationally healthy (ServiceAvailable=True) while epistemically degraded (CalibrationBad=True): OperationalHealth != EpistemicValidity -- 'a model endpoint returning HTTP 200 does not mean ModelCorrect; it only means ComputationExecuted'. Experiment 15: a fully available model service with systematically biased predictions correctly yields OperationalStatus=Healthy but EpistemicStatus=Degraded -- PASS, giving a two-dimensional Status=(Operational,Epistemic), e.g. (Healthy,Degraded).
invariants: OperationalHealth ≠ EpistemicValidity; a responsive service is never equated with a correct model

rows.anchor: Model governance lifecycle; automatic-promotion rejected: Model performance != Model authorization
rows.statement: Gives the model governance lifecycle Candidate -> Validated -> Approved -> Production -> Degraded -> Suspended -> Retired, each transition needing explicit conditions. Experiment 16: a newly trained model reaching 95% accuracy attempting Candidate->Production automatically is rejected because governance requires human/automated independent validation -- PromotionRejected -- PASS, giving the governance principle Model performance != Model authorization, exactly analogous to Decision != Authorization.
invariants: Model performance ≠ Model authorization

lineage_claims.quote: Exactly analogous to: Decision ≠ Authorization.

rows.anchor: Governed self-healing: DetectDrift->Retrain->Validate->Candidate, never automatic Production; controlled self-improvement loop
rows.statement: Asks whether KnowledgeOS can automatically retrain a degraded model: DetectDrift -> Retrain -> Validate -> Candidate, but never automatically Production unless governance explicitly permits it. Experiment 17: drift detected, system retrains, NewModelStatus=Candidate not Production -- PASS. States this gives 'Learning without UncontrolledAuthority', formalized as a self-improvement loop Outcome -> Evaluation -> DriftDetection -> Learning -> CandidateModel -> Validation -> GovernedPromotion -- 'much safer than Outcome -> AI retrains itself -> Production'.
invariants: a self-retrained model never automatically reaches Production; governed promotion is always required

lineage_claims.quote: This is much safer than: Outcome → AI retrains itself → Production.

rows.anchor: Executable Models != permanently Validated Models; context-dependent Valid(M,t,D,A); eight-conjunct Correctness(KOS) equation
rows.statement: States the provisional principle: Executable Models must not be treated as permanently Validated Models -- validity is Contextual + Temporal + EvidenceDependent, formalized as Valid(M,t,D,A) depending on time, data, and assumptions (Valid(M) alone is incomplete). Extends the model-risk dependency chain Evidence -> Assumptions -> Model -> Prediction -> Decision -> Action -> Outcome, every edge potentially carrying Uncertainty and Provenance, with impact propagation from a degraded Model through Predictions -> Decisions -> Actions (again Affected != Invalid, requiring domain-specific reassessment) -- 'the system can answer not just what do we know, but which decisions depend on knowledge or models that have changed'. Extends the running correctness formula to Correctness = Safety ∧ Liveness ∧ Compositionality ∧ Concurrency ∧ EpistemicIntegrity ∧ DecisionIntegrity ∧ CausalIntegrity ∧ ModelValidity.

lineage_claims.quote: Our working model is now: Correctness = Safety ∧ Liveness ∧ Compositionality ∧ Concurrency ∧ EpistemicIntegrity ∧ DecisionIntegrity ∧ CausalIntegrity ∧ ModelValidity.

rows.anchor: Step 64 verdict PASS WITH STRONG ARCHITECTURAL REFINEMENT; six required capabilities; governed computational loop diagram; opens Step 65 on multi-agent epistemic independence
rows.statement: Declares STEP 64 -- PASS WITH STRONG ARCHITECTURAL REFINEMENT, requiring Temporal Model Validity, Model Lineage, Assumption Tracking, Drift Detection, Independent Evaluation, and Governed Model Promotion. Depicts the governed computational loop Evidence -> Knowledge -> Models -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action -> Outcome -> Evaluation -> {Model Validation, Knowledge Update} -> New Candidate, with the loop never allowed to bypass governance. Opens Step 65 (Multi-Agent Epistemic Independence and Error Propagation): what happens when evidence itself is AI-generated (AI_A -> Evidence -> AI_B -> Knowledge -> Decision, potentially cyclically AI_A -> AI_B -> AI_C -> AI_A), creating epistemic feedback loops and correlated AI errors -- investigating genuine agent independence, correlated-error propagation, AI-generated-vs-external evidence, whether multiple agreeing agents actually increase confidence, circular citation, model-family common-mode failure, and preventing repetition from manufacturing truth -- framed as testing whether multi-agent KnowledgeOS scales epistemically, not merely computationally.

sources.note: The Recommendation domain (issuance, decision, rationale) under live observational discovery.

rows.anchor: RD-1 | A recommendation is immutable once issued; responses live in SEPARATE records
rows.statement: A Recommendation is immutable once issued, with dedicated response records (decisions.jsonl) kept structurally separate from the issuance record.

rows.anchor: RD-2 | Identity = (rule, subject) — duplicates cannot exist while open
rows.statement: A Recommendation's identity is the pair (rule, subject); while a recommendation on that pair is open, no duplicate can be issued, confirmed by a re-run producing zero new records.

rows.anchor: RD-3 | Rules produce structurally honest silence (absence of grounds → absence of advice)
rows.statement: Recommendation rules are designed to stay silent when they lack grounds to fire, observed four times in Run 1 (e.g. insufficient history, flat CBO), rather than issuing speculative advice.

rows.anchor: RD-4 | identity may need THREE layers: RecommendationDefinition / Instance / Revision
rows.statement: A staged hypothesis proposes that Recommendation identity may eventually need three layers (Definition/Instance/Revision) because (rule,subject) dedup cannot answer whether a rule changed, whether re-issuance after changed conditions is warranted, or whether v1-ignored/v2-accepted should be distinguished; held at 'think, never implement, until a real question requires it'.

rows.anchor: RD-5 | recommendations accumulate AGE — and age is already computable from existing timestamps
rows.statement: Recommendation age (time-to-decision) is computable purely from existing issued/decided timestamps with no new schema fields; validated when Run 2 computed a real 6.5-hour time-to-decision from existing data.

rows.anchor: RD-6 | ACTOR PROVENANCE GAP: the decision record's actor stamps the git user, but the decider was the AI at the user's direction
rows.statement: When an AI participates in a decision at a user's direction, the decision record's actor field stamps the git user identity, obscuring who-executed versus who-authorized; only the free-text rationale comment carries the honest attribution today, flagged as a real modeling question once a second AI-mediated decision occurs.

rows.anchor: RD-7 | A recommendation CAN currently be decided twice: two identical ACCEPTED records exist for REC-eaf245474a
rows.statement: A genuine anomaly: a session interruption produced two identical ACCEPTED decision records for the same recommendation, empirically answering (by accident) that recommendations can currently be re-decided unguarded, and skewing a naive dashboard record count; the fix for this is deliberately deferred until the domain semantics (exactly-once vs last-wins) are decided, so as not to prematurely encode a guard.

rows.anchor: NONE YET — insufficient evidence, said explicitly.
rows.statement: The DDD classification of Recommendation (Application Service / Domain Service / Aggregate / Domain Capability / Process Manager) is explicitly refused for insufficient evidence after only one day of issuance with zero responses; the shape currently resembles 'an event with a process around it' more than an aggregate, pending accumulation of decisions, rationales, and outcomes.

rows.anchor: DECIDING observed for the first time — ACCEPTED with reason code + comment
rows.statement: Run 2 recorded the first-ever Decide action on a recommendation (ACCEPTED, reason code IMMEDIATE_VALUE), upgrading several ubiquitous-language terms from vocabulary-only to observed-exercised.

rows.anchor: Impact: STILL insufficient — the first learning event is 3/5 complete (recommendation ✓ decision ✓ rationale ✓ · commit ✗ outcome ✗)
rows.statement: Even after the first real decision, the KnowledgeOS-impact learning event remains only 3 of 5 complete (missing a real code change and a post-commit metric delta), so impact measurement stays insufficient evidence.

rows.anchor: Re-run this discovery when: the first decision lands · every ~10 decisions thereafter · any anomaly appears in practice.
rows.statement: The observation protocol commits to re-running this discovery instrument only on evidence triggers (first decision, every ~10 decisions, or an anomaly), never on a schedule, and forbids ML/ranking/confidence-scoring/adaptive behavior unless deterministic v1 demonstrably fails.

rows.anchor: Recommendation lifecycle — class A, exercised once ... 8 recommendations remain open since 2026-08-04. The single closed loop returned INCONCLUSIVE ... the same recommendation was decided twice ... with near-identical rationales
rows.statement: The full recommendation->decision->outcome->assessment chain is implemented and has been exercised exactly once end-to-end: 10 issued -> 2 decision rows (1 unique recommendation) -> 1 outcome -> 1 assessment (verdict INCONCLUSIVE, 'only 1 commits since decision, min 3'); 8 recommendations remain open since 2026-08-04; the same recommendation was decided twice with near-identical rationales, which the mechanism permits (classifying by latest) but the duplicate is still visible in the record. DASHBOARD.md itself frames the drop-off as 'a finding, not a failure -- an organizational mirror.'

rows.anchor: the determination lineage ... p <- R <- E <- O with C,t,M attached to the determination. Then tomorrow O' arrives and challenges p. We need to reconstruct: Why did KnowledgeOS believe/accept p yesterday? That is not merely uncertainty. That is epistemic provenance.
rows.statement: Proposes a deeper candidate Kernel invariant not yet emphasized by the prior synthesis: the determination lineage -- for a determined proposition p, the chain p<-R<-E<-O (determination from reasoning from evidence from observation) with context/time/method (C,t,M) attached; when a new observation O' later challenges p, the Kernel must be able to reconstruct why p was believed/accepted at the earlier time. This is termed epistemic provenance, distinct from mere uncertainty, and may be more fundamental to the Kernel than any particular probability distribution.
missing: formal definition of the lineage data structure

rows.anchor: Take exactly one real proposition. ... p = "System X satisfies requirement R at time t". ... Regime 1 Classical logic ... Regime 6 Fuzzy/many-valued logic. Then compare: What survives? ... Do they identify the same proposition? ... Can the result be revised when new evidence arrives?
rows.statement: Proposes a concrete experiment: take one real proposition (p='System X satisfies requirement R at time t'), preserve a fixed substrate (observations, sources, timestamps, context, actors, statements, previous determinations, relations, applicable rules/methods), and run it through six regimes (classical logic, Bayesian inference, Dempster-Shafer, non-monotonic reasoning, argumentation, fuzzy/many-valued logic), then compare what survives across eight questions: do they identify the same proposition, use the same observations, preserve the same provenance, identify the same conflicts, identify the same possible states, preserve the same dependency relations, permit reconstruction of why the result was reached, and permit revision when new evidence arrives. Claimed to be more informative than further abstract architecture discussion.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS is not trying to determine which evidence-combination mathematics is universally correct. Instead: KnowledgeOS must preserve enough epistemic substrate that different valid determination regimes can independently reconstruct and evaluate the same phenomenon. ... rows.statement: Sharpens the research position: KnowledgeOS is not trying to determine which evidence-combination mathematics is universally correct; instead it must preserve enough epistemic substrate that different valid determination regimes can independently reconstruct and evaluate the same phenomenon. The hardest unresolved question is now: what is the minimum substrate required to reconstruct a conditional determination -- judged closer to the actual Kernel question than asking what should be stored as 'Knowledge'.

rows.anchor: Today: "Nexus is migration ready." Tomorrow: A critical dependency is discovered. Now: "Nexus is not migration ready." Was yesterday's knowledge necessarily wrong? No. It may have been the correct determination given the evidence available at that time. ... Why did we believe this at T1? ... Why did we change our conclusion at T2? That is why time, history and provenance become important.
rows.statement: Problem 5 (today's correct answer can become tomorrow's wrong answer): a migration-readiness determination that is true at T1 can be revised to false at T2 when a critical dependency is discovered, without yesterday's determination having been wrong -- it may have been correct given the evidence available at that time; the system must preserve both Knowledge-at-T1 and Knowledge-at-T2 and be able to answer 'why did we believe this at T1' and 'why did we change our conclusion at T2', which is why time, history and provenance matter.
invariants: a later revision does not retroactively make an earlier, evidence-consistent determination wrong

rows.anchor: The reference itself has an epistemic history. We cannot simply store: RequiredVersion=3.85. We potentially need to know: Why do we accept 3.85 as the reference? ... Evidence -> Justification -> Trusted Statement -> Reference State -> Comparison -> New Determination. ... Trust is not the same as truth. ... Statement -> Reason -> Logic -> Justification -> Trust/Acceptance.
rows.statement: The reference/ideal state is itself knowledge requiring its own epistemic history: not merely RequiredVersion=3.85, but why 3.85 is accepted (who stated it, what evidence/justification, what trust rule, when valid, who accepted it, has it since changed), giving the recursive chain Evidence -> Justification -> Trusted Statement -> Reference State -> Comparison -> New Determination. Trust is not the same as truth: a trusted source's statement must preserve why it is trusted (Statement -> Reason -> Logic -> Justification -> Trust/Acceptance), not merely who said it.
invariants: a reference/ideal state is never stored as a bare value -- its own justification chain must be preserved
trust is never conflated with truth

rows.anchor: The owner's decision is itself a new fact/dimension in the evolving state, rather than something that should overwrite the previous conflicting knowledge. ... D_{t+1}=D_t union {d_ownerDecision}. ... The owner's decision does not make the security evidence "true" and the architecture evidence "false." ... KnowledgeOS preserves the evidence and the decisions made from that evidence; it does not collapse the history into the latest decision.
rows.statement: An owner's resolving decision (e.g. 'treat Nexus as non-compliant, security position prioritized') is itself a new fact/dimension added to the evolving state, D_{t+1}=D_t union {d_ownerDecision} (with value, reason, authority, time), not something that overwrites or erases the prior conflicting evidence -- the security and architecture evidence both remain part of the Knowledge state; KnowledgeOS preserves the evidence and the decisions made from it rather than collapsing history into the latest decision. Whether the decision describes reality or becomes a new rule/reference for future evaluation is resolved as: it becomes a new organizational fact/reference that future observations must be considered against, without automatically overriding a later change in underlying conditions (e.g. the security issue being fixed does not retroactively change the recorded decision).
invariants: a resolving decision is added as a new fact alongside prior evidence, never as an overwrite/deletion of that evidence

rationale_evidence.statement: An owner's resolving decision (e.g. 'treat Nexus as non-compliant, security position prioritized') is itself a new fact/dimension added to the evolving state, D_{t+1}=D_t union {d_ownerDecision} (with value, reason, authority, time), not something that overwrites or erases the prior conflicting evidence -- the security and architecture evidence both remain part of the Knowledge state; KnowledgeOS preserves the evidence and the decisions made from it rather than collapsing history into the latest decision. Whether the decision describes reality or becomes a new rule/reference for future evaluation is resolved as: it becomes a new organizational fact/reference that future observations must be considered against, without automatically overriding a later change in underlying conditions (e.g. the security issue being fixed does not retroactively change the recorded decision).

rationale_evidence.statement: Called 'perhaps the most architecturally important discovery': determination is recursive — F_1 is determined from observations, F_2 from F_1, F_3 from F_2, etc., creating a determination history O->F_1->F_2->F_3->...; if F_3 is later challenged, reconstruction requires tracing F_3<-F_2<-F_1<-O. rows.statement: The Qualify cycle (to qualify an observation into evidence you need a policy; the policy is knowledge content; that content is an assertion; that assertion is justified by evidence) is the single genuine unrecorded circularity in the theory — v0.2's R-1 stratification terminates the loop about *changing* policy but says nothing about *using* a policy inside qualification, and the human-act externalization does not help either since a human act authorises a policy, it does not qualify an observation. Whether it is a legitimate Knaster-Tarski fixed point cannot even be tested because Qualify has no body.

The pipeline survives only as a description of execution sequence, not dependency order.

rows.anchor: We should therefore never model governance simply as: allowed = true/false. We need at least the semantic distinction: Required, Permitted, Forbidden, Unknown and potentially: Recommended, Discouraged.
rows.statement: Proposes a deontic-modal governance vocabulary (Required, Permitted, Forbidden, Unknown, and potentially Recommended/Discouraged) as necessary to replace a naive boolean allowed=true/false governance model, since 'positive permission' Permitted(a), 'obligation' Required(a), and 'prohibition' Forbidden(a) are argued to be distinct semantic categories, closer to a policy/dharma model than an IF-condition-THEN-execute command system.

rows.anchor: A workflow should not assume: Decision => Action. Instead: Decision -> {ACT, REFRAIN, DEFER, ESCALATE, SEEK MORE KNOWLEDGE}. ... Insufficient Evidence => Do Not Determine and perhaps => SeekMoreEvidence. That is epistemic restraint.
rows.statement: 'Do nothing' (and deferral/escalation/seeking more evidence) must be first-class Decision outcomes rather than an implicit fallback: Decision -> {ACT, REFRAIN, DEFER, ESCALATE, SEEK MORE KNOWLEDGE}; when evidence is insufficient a KnowledgeOS-governed agent should conclude 'Do Not Determine' / 'SeekMoreEvidence' rather than force an answer -- termed 'epistemic restraint'.

rows.anchor: We have already established that: Evidence not=> Truth. Now Chapter 4 gives us another principle: Knowledge not=> Action. There must be an intermediate judgment: Knowledge -> Judgment -> Action/Restraint.
rows.statement: By analogy to the already-established 'Evidence does not imply Truth' principle, Chapter 4 is read as supplying a parallel principle 'Knowledge does not imply Action', requiring an intermediate Judgment stage: Knowledge -> Judgment -> Action/Restraint.
dependencies: Evidence does not imply Truth (deterministic assurance principle)

rows.anchor: Principle IV-A -- Wisdom of action and restraint: A governed system must be capable of determining both what should be done and what should not be done. Therefore: Decision -> {Act, Refrain, Defer, Escalate, Investigate}.
rows.statement: Names and records 'Principle IV-A -- Wisdom of action and restraint': a governed system must be able to determine both what should be done and what should not be done, formalized as Decision -> {Act, Refrain, Defer, Escalate, Investigate}.
invariants: Principle IV-A

rows.anchor: The actor must know the limits of its own knowledge. This is perhaps the most important principle for AI. An agent should be able to say: I know this. I do not know this. I previously knew this but cannot currently reconstruct it. ... That is epistemically mature architecture.
rows.statement: States a third principle, considered possibly the most important for AI: 'the actor must know the limits of its own knowledge', illustrated by a required repertoire of self-report statements (I know this / I do not know this / I previously knew this but cannot currently reconstruct it / the system has historical evidence for this / the evidence is insufficient for action / the action is prohibited / the action requires authority), termed 'epistemically mature architecture'.
missing: formal encoding of the self-report repertoire

rows.anchor: HISTORICAL LINEAGE -> KNOWLEDGE -> INQUIRY -> EVIDENCE -> DETERMINATION -> WISDOM -> (SHOULD DO / SHOULD NOT DO) -> DECISION -> (ACT/DEFER/REFRAIN) -> EXECUTION -> OBSERVATION -> NEW KNOWLEDGE/UPDATE, and above all of it: PROVENANCE + LINEAGE
rows.statement: Revises the KnowledgeOS pipeline diagram (previously Knowledge->Inquiry->Evidence->Determination->Decision->Action) into a richer chain: HISTORICAL LINEAGE -> KNOWLEDGE -> INQUIRY -> EVIDENCE -> DETERMINATION -> WISDOM -> {SHOULD DO, SHOULD NOT DO} -> DECISION -> {ACT, DEFER, REFRAIN} -> EXECUTION -> OBSERVATION -> NEW KNOWLEDGE/UPDATE, with PROVENANCE + LINEAGE positioned as an overarching background layer.

sources.note: Gap-discovery comparison of KnowledgeOS against Shannon information theory (entropy/mutual-information/KL-divergence, all functionals of a probability distribution), its measure-free partition-lattice layer, and semantic-information theories (Bar-Hillel-Carnap/Dretske exclusion-of-possibilities, Floridi's veridicality thesis). Rated 'THE WEAKEST FIT OF THE FIVE': the quantitative layer (entropy/mutual-information/KL) is wholly unavailable since (Omega,F,P) has zero occurrences and Step-282's T-3 ruling declines probability as required; the word 'entropy' appears 87 times in the corpus with 0 ratified uses, so none can be genuine Shannon entropy (recorded as falsifiable hypothesis IT-H1, not asserted); Floridi's veridicality thesis (information is necessarily truthful) directly contradicts the corpus's boxed 'Admission is not a truth function' result, since a Refuted assertion is a first-class corpus member that would be inexpressible under veridicality; and Dretske's channel-based information-carrying definition requires a conditional-probability-1 condition and a background-knowledge index that KnowledgeOS's Evidence(O,P,C,R)/Qualify (TG-14, no body) cannot supply. The one positive finding: Zero(K,G,EC) fits the measure-free partition/coverage LATTICE exactly as an antichain of unsatisfied requirements in a finite lattice (an ORDER, not a NUMBER) -- matching the corpus's own boxed 'Zero != simple subtraction' and independently corroborated by an executed zero_reference.py counterexample (two work plans with equal gap-counts |gaps(A)|=|gaps(B)|=2 that are nonetheless different plans, proving Zero is not a cardinality). Five falsifiable hypotheses IT-H1..IT-H5.

rows.anchor: Zero <-> an antichain of unsatisfied requirements in a finite lattice — an ORDER, not a NUMBER
rows.statement: Finds Zero(K,G,EC) (evaluated over a finite requirement set with sufficiency rules Gamma, returning one of ten statuses per requirement, boxed 'Zero != simple subtraction') fits Shannon's measure-free structural layer: requirements generate a finite meet-semilattice under partition refinement, and Zero is the set of requirements not yet in the satisfied down-set -- an antichain in a lattice, an ORDER rather than a NUMBER; the corpus's own boxed rejection of simple subtraction is exactly the statement that this lattice is not a measure, stated without the vocabulary.

rows.anchor: |gaps(A)| = |gaps(B)| = 2, yet A != B as work plans — any count/scalar conflates them. That is a demonstration that Zero is not a cardinality, i.e. not a measure.
rows.statement: Reports an executed corroboration from zero_reference.py: two work plans A and B have equal gap-counts (|gaps(A)|=|gaps(B)|=2) yet are different work plans, so any scalar/cardinality summary of Zero conflates them -- an independent demonstration (found by running code, not by information-theoretic argument) that Zero cannot be a cardinality/measure, agreeing with the information-theory finding.

experiment.hypothesis: Zero(K,G,EC) can be summarized by a scalar count of unsatisfied requirements
experiment.setup: two work plans A and B with different unsatisfied-requirement sets but equal set sizes
experiment.assumptions: a scalar gap-count would be a sufficient summary of Zero
experiment.method: execute zero_reference.py and compare gap-count vs actual plan content
experiment.result: |gaps(A)|=|gaps(B)|=2 while A and B differ as work plans
experiment.interpretation: any count/scalar conflates distinct Zero states
experiment.limitations: not stated
experiment.conclusion: Zero is not a cardinality, i.e. not a measure

rows.anchor: H, I, D_KL are all functionals of a probability distribution. (Omega,F,P) as a triple: 0 occurrences in both lanes; T-3 rules probability not required. Shannon's quantitative layer is unavailable to KnowledgeOS by the same ruling that declined probability.
rows.statement: Decisive incompatibility: Shannon entropy, mutual information and KL-divergence are all functionals of a declared probability distribution (Omega,F,P), which has zero occurrences in the corpus and was explicitly ruled unnecessary by Step 282's T-3; therefore the entire Shannon quantitative layer is unavailable to KnowledgeOS by the same ruling that declined probability, leaving only the measure-free lattice layer (which supports refinement/coverage/gap structure but no number).

rows.anchor: entropy appears 87 times in the corpus, 0 ratified. ... every one of those 87 uses is either (a) metaphorical, (b) about an external regime not adopted, or (c) an error.
rows.statement: Measures 87 corpus occurrences of the word 'entropy'/'entropy H(' with zero ratified formal uses, and infers (recorded as unaudited hypothesis IT-H1, not an asserted fact) that every occurrence must be metaphorical, about an unadopted external regime, or an error, since no probability distribution exists anywhere in the corpus to license a genuine Shannon entropy computation; classifies this as the same defect class as prior findings about quantitative vocabulary used without the structure that licenses it, noting the corpus's own Shannon extraction already warns 'information is not meaning is not knowledge.'

rows.anchor: An assertion with Sigma=(0,1) Refuted is a first-class member of A and, on the veridicality thesis, carries no semantic information at all. Adopting Floridi would make Refuted inexpressible.
rows.statement: Decisive incompatibility: Floridi's veridicality thesis holds semantic information is necessarily truthful (false 'information' is not information), but the corpus's Closure-03 result 'Admission is not a truth function' deliberately retains Refuted assertions as first-class members of A; adopting Floridi's thesis would make Refuted assertions inexpressible -- classified as the same shape of error as adopting S5 veridicality for Sigma in the DEL comparison document.

rows.anchor: Dretske's definition is strictly stronger — it requires (i) a conditional probability, (ii) its value to be exactly 1, and (iii) a background-knowledge index k. KnowledgeOS supplies none.
rows.statement: Finds Dretske's information-carrying definition (signal r carries the information that s is F iff the conditional probability of s-is-F given r and receiver prior knowledge k equals exactly 1) strictly stronger than what KnowledgeOS's Evidence(O,P,C,R) (a relevance relation under a rule) can supply, especially since the verification-lane Qualify function has no implemented body (TG-14); concludes Evidence is not Dretskean information-carrying and cannot become so without reversing the T-3 no-probability ruling.

rows.anchor: a way to distinguish not-asked from asked-and-empty | tolerance of contradictory signals as a state | provenance/authority | a goal state | non-veridical carriers ... a source distribution | a channel | an empirical relational structure | a code/compression notion
rows.statement: Lists missing primitives on the information-theory side needed to host KnowledgeOS (a way to distinguish not-asked from asked-and-empty, since a sample-space partition has no 'unasked' cell -- the same defect class found against DEL; tolerance of contradictory signals as a state, for Conflict; provenance/authority, for governed admission; a goal state, for Ideal State; non-veridical carriers, for Refuted assertions) and on the KnowledgeOS side needed to host information theory (a source distribution -- 0 occurrences, declined by T-3; a channel -- no P(O|phi) anywhere; an empirical relational structure -- corpus finding G-12 blocks any numeric information measure independently of T-3; a code/compression notion -- absent and not obviously needed).

rows.anchor: IT-H1 ... IT-H2 ... IT-H3 ... IT-H4 ... IT-H5
rows.statement: States five falsifiable hypotheses: IT-H1 (all 87 corpus 'entropy' uses are metaphorical/regime-external/erroneous, falsified by exhibiting one that declares (Omega,F,P) and computes H over it); IT-H2 (Zero is a lattice antichain, not a measure -- no scalar summary preserves the ten-status distinction, already partly corroborated by zero_reference.py); IT-H3 (no distance-to-Ideal-State satisfying Q12 is definable without a metric or distribution, neither of which exists); IT-H4 (adopting Floridi veridicality would make Refuted inexpressible); IT-H5 (Evidence(O,P,C,R) is strictly weaker than Dretskean information-carrying, falsified by deriving Dretske's conditional-probability-1 condition from Qualify, currently impossible since Qualify has no body).

rows.anchor: THE WEAKEST FIT OF THE FIVE — the quantitative layer is unavailable and the semantic layer contradicts a boxed corpus result ... What this analysis adds is that the residue is a lattice, and that Zero is already sitting in it.
rows.statement: Final verdict: information theory is the weakest fit of the five external theories compared in this series -- no entropy/mutual-information/KL is available (all require the declined distribution), Floridi's veridicality thesis directly contradicts the corpus's Admission-is-not-a-truth-function result, and Dretske needs a channel and independence/prior structure the corpus lacks -- but the measure-free partition/coverage lattice does exactly fit Zero, and the corpus's own 2026-08-25 conclusion ('information is not meaning is not knowledge') is endorsed as correct; the analysis's own addition is identifying that the surviving residue is specifically a LATTICE, and that Zero already sits in it.

rows.anchor: Temporal knowledge is the biggest weakness in the current architecture ... EKS/AIP: only 2/218 transitions carry any date. ... It does not conclude that KnowledgeOS must implement bitemporal storage. It concludes: UNKNOWN whether a richer temporal model is needed.
rows.statement: DeepSeek identifies temporal knowledge as the biggest architectural gap found: EKS/AIP transitions carry a date field in only 2/218 cases, and PKS has supersession semantics but lacks a timestamp dimension, so the architecture often cannot answer 'what was authoritative at time T?', only 'what is recorded now?'. Explicitly does NOT conclude bitemporal storage is required; concludes UNKNOWN whether a richer temporal model is needed -- 'that distinction is architecturally excellent.'
missing: whether richer temporal model needed

rows.anchor: The persistence inversion ... GRANTS + TRANSITIONS 🔴 NO 🔴 NO 🔴 NO (authority · ownership · lineage — the evidence of who was permitted to do what) ... .claude/runtime/ is the ONLY excluded subdirectory of .claude/
rows.statement: The persistence inversion: ADRs, reviews, and observation streams are durable/git-tracked/history-preserving/time-reconstructable, while grants+transitions -- the record of who was permitted to do what -- are NOT durable, NOT historied, and NOT temporally reconstructable, because .claude/runtime/ is gitignored (the only excluded subdirectory of .claude/, excluded twice, at lines 25 and 32, deliberately per registry.yaml AST-015 notes). Consequences: no git history for a grant/transition insertion; single-host authoritative state (any other clone folds to UNRESOLVABLE); no backup/replication/integrity check.

rows.anchor: Measured this session: 2 of 218 transitions (0.9%) carry any time-like field ... Authority in EKS is durably stated and completely un-timed. ... 'Reports are ephemeral: re-run before acting, never cache (staleness is uncomputable — the record carries no transition timestamps, D-1).'
rows.statement: Temporal reconstructability is class E, MISSING: only 2/218 transitions (0.9%) carry any time-like field (day granularity only); ordering is by per-record seq alone, with no relation across records; combined with no git history, questions such as 'when was grant G-X registered?', 'which grants were in force when act Y occurred?', or 'did the handoff precede the human act?' are unanswerable by any mechanism -- 'authority in EKS is durably stated and completely un-timed.'

rows.anchor: There is no event architecture in EKS. Class E — MISSING. ... 'Transition' | a persisted fact, not a published event. Nothing subscribes. Governance discovers other processes' transitions by re-folding, not by notification
rows.statement: No event architecture exists in EKS (class E, verified by exhaustive absence of event type/bus/broker/publisher/subscriber/store/outbox/transport/schema). What exists instead: Triggers are synchronous adapters producing a ChangeSet DTO with no message/queue/delivery-guarantee; a Transition is a persisted fact, not a published event -- nothing subscribes, and governance discovers other processes' transitions 'by re-folding, not by notification' (first-hand: six transitions recorded by other windows during a single Governance session were discovered only by re-fold). Integration style stated plainly: 'a shared-file integration architecture with synchronous in-process calls.'

rows.anchor: 23 / 30 concurrent-append trials silently lost a transition
rows.statement: Erratum E-1: the prior claim that dense/monotonic seq numbers make omission mechanically detectable is WITHDRAWN. MIGRATION-PLAN SS1.3 AMD3 CL-1 reproduced concurrent-append trials: 23/30 silently lost a transition (the losing process exited 0 reporting {ok:true,seq:2}) while every survivor stayed dense and monotonic (the clobbering writer reuses the lost writer's sequence number); the write is atomic per write (tmp+rename) but the read-modify-write is NOT atomic (no lock, lease, CAS or version check). Corrects P3 SS8.1.

experiment.hypothesis: dense, monotonic seq numbers prove completeness of the append log
experiment.setup: concurrent-append trials against workflow-state.php's read-modify-write append path
experiment.assumptions: atomic per-write (tmp+rename) was believed to imply atomic read-modify-write
experiment.method: reproduced concurrent appends and inspected resulting seq sequences (per MIGRATION-PLAN SS1.3 AMD3 CL-1)
experiment.result: 23 of 30 trials silently lost a transition while every survivor was dense and monotonic
experiment.interpretation: density/monotonicity of seq is NOT a completeness proof; read-modify-write lacks locking/CAS/versioning
experiment.limitations: reported second-hand via the MIGRATION-PLAN, not independently re-run in this document
experiment.conclusion: the current persistence mechanism does not provide completeness merely from dense sequence numbers

rows.statement: Erratum E-2: 'exactly one writer (workflow-state.php)' is WITHDRAWN as a structural guarantee -- it is only the currently identified primary writer. A second write-capable path exists: session-resolve.php:90 reads getenv('KOS_MECHANISM_PATH') and :103 executes the environment-named program via proc_open, handing it the authority-record directory as an argument (:156) -- a write-capable substitution path through a component whose own bytes contain no write call. Corrects P3 SS8.1/SS9.3.

sources.note: S0708's application of Berger & Luckmann's The Social Construction of Reality to the KnowledgeOS model: separates three questions (what is the state / what do we epistemically know about it / what does an organization socially accept as knowledge about it), introduces the social/institutional legitimation layer (objectivation, legitimation, institutionalization, distribution, maintenance, internalization), warns against reification (treating an institutional determination as a decontextualized 'thing' once its evidence/reasoning/conflict/time are forgotten), and proposes three dimension categories D^state/D^epistemic/D^social as a research hypothesis. Distinct from epistemic-qualification-conditions (S0707, which is about individual epistemic conditions for knowledge) -- this is about organizational/social legitimation of knowledge.

rows.anchor: Berger & Luckmann define knowledge sociologically as the certainty that phenomena are real and have specific characteristics, while explicitly studying whatever a society treats as knowledge, regardless of ultimate validity. ... 1. What is the state? 2. What do we know about the state? 3. What does an organization/society accept as knowledge about the state?
rows.statement: Berger & Luckmann define knowledge sociologically as the certainty that phenomena are real and have specific characteristics, studying whatever a society treats as knowledge regardless of ultimate validity; this adds a third question that must not be collapsed with the other two: (1) what is the state (dimensions/values/relationships), (2) what do we epistemically know about the state (truth/belief/ability/safety/justification/entitlement/recognition/testimony), and (3) what does an organization/society accept as knowledge about the state (social production, objectivation, legitimation, institutionalization, distribution, maintenance, internalization).
invariants: the state layer, the individual epistemic layer, and the social/institutional legitimation layer are three distinct questions, never collapsed

rows.anchor: Who or what makes a determination socially legitimate? ... Governance / institutional legitimacy ... Organizational knowledge: "Nexus is not compliant." The last step is not merely a mathematical calculation. It depends on institutionalized rules and socially established meanings. ... legitimation as giving cognitive validity and normative legitimacy to institutional meanings.
rows.statement: Adds a governance/institutional-legitimacy step after determination: 'Nexus is not compliant' as organizational knowledge is not merely a mathematical calculation from a determination -- it depends on institutionalized rules and socially established meanings (legitimation giving cognitive validity and normative legitimacy to institutional meanings), directly relevant to governance/architecture work.

rows.anchor: Physical/technical state: What Nexus actually is. Expected/target state: What the organization says Nexus should be. rows.statement: Distinguishes four non-identical reference spaces previously conflated under 'ideal state': the physical/technical state (what Nexus actually is), the expected/target state (what the organization says it should be), the socially legitimate state (what the organization currently accepts as the valid interpretation), and the decision state (what the owner decided to do) -- a major unresolved issue, since 'ideal state' must never be automatically equated with 'organizationally approved state'.

rows.anchor: State dimensions: properties of the observed object/system, e.g. Version=2.69. rows.statement: Proposes three dimension categories that can coexist without being the same kind of dimension: state dimensions (properties of the observed object, e.g. Version=2.69), epistemic dimensions (properties concerning our knowledge of the state, e.g. confidence in the version observation), and social/governance dimensions (properties concerning institutional acceptance, e.g. an owner decision) -- formalized as D*=D^state union D^epistemic union D^social, explicitly a research hypothesis, not an established fact.
missing: validation that these three categories are jointly exhaustive/non-overlapping

rows.anchor: They explicitly warn about reification: treating human products as if they were things. ... Nexus.status = NON_COMPLIANT. Six months later everyone forgets: who determined it; why; based on which evidence; ... The organizational decision has been turned into a thing. That is exactly the danger of reification.
rows.statement: Berger & Luckmann's reification warning (treating human products as if they were things) applies directly to KnowledgeOS: storing a bare 'Nexus.status = NON_COMPLIANT' and losing who determined it, why, on what evidence, under which rule, when, and against which conflicting evidence turns a socially/organizationally produced determination into a decontextualized 'thing' -- exactly the danger the model must guard against by preserving evidence+reasoning+conflicting information+owner decision+time.
invariants: an organizational determination is never stored as a bare value stripped of who/why/evidence/rule/time/conflict

rows.statement: Declares the pivot point of the whole Gita-kernel track: stop adding philosophical interpretation, start systematic operator discovery, framed as the real engineering question (what operations can the Kernel perform, under what conditions, preserving what invariants). Proposes a five-phase discovery pipeline: Strategic Discovery -> Tactical Discovery -> Formal Operator Catalogue -> Simulation -> Canonicalization, with the discipline that operators are discovered first and never declared canonical merely because the Gita suggests them.

rows.anchor: Kernel: (K_t,O_t,C_t) -> (K_{t+1},E_t) ... Buddhi sits inside this transformation ... Input -> Buddhi -> Kernel Operation -> K_{t+1}. The Kernel does not blindly transform knowledge. It must determine: Is this admissible? Is it new? Is it contradictory? Does it strengthen an existing proposition? Does it invalidate something? Does it require qualification? Does it change a dimension? Does it require action? Does it merely represent uncertainty?
rows.statement: Models the Kernel as a bounded domain: Kernel: (K_t,O_t,C_t) -> (K_{t+1},E_t) [current state, observations/input, contextual constraints -> resulting state, evidence/audit], with Buddhi sitting inside the transformation (Input -> Buddhi -> Kernel Operation -> K_{t+1}), enumerating nine discrimination questions the Kernel must ask (admissible? new? contradictory? strengthens? invalidates? needs qualification? changes a dimension? requires action? represents uncertainty?).

rows.statement: Names the first two of nine candidate operator families for systematic (not philosophy-first) discovery: SD-1 Acquisition operators (Acquire, Observe, Receive, Detect, Discover), reinforcing Observation != Proposition != Knowledge with a worked HTTP-500 example; SD-2 Discrimination operators, the 'Buddhi family' (Distinguish, Compare, Classify, Separate, Accept, Reject, Defer, Contradict), noting P1!=P2 does not imply P1 is false -- Buddhi must distinguish seven distinct relations: different, contradictory, more specific, superseding, compatible, incomparable, unknown.

Derivation != Corroboration. ... SD-4 Knowledge revision operators: Update, Revise, Supersede, Correct, Invalidate, Retract, Expire ... K_t != K_{t+1} is normal rather than exceptional ... SD-4 Knowledge revision operators (Update, Revise, Supersede, Correct, Invalidate, Retract, Expire), grounded in K_t != K_{t+1} being normal, with a proposed central invariant that K_{t+1} must preserve sufficient history to explain the K_t->K_{t+1} transition, explicitly connecting the operator-discovery problem to the corpus's existing H/replay structure.

rows.statement: SD-6 Relationship operators (Member, Relate, Compare, Contradict, Support, Depend, Supersede, Derive, Trace), raising whether the relation component R is a data structure or itself the result of Kernel operations. SD-9 Action operators, distinguishing Knowledge transformation from World transformation (since the verification lane treats Action/Event/Policy as external to the epistemic projection), giving a closed epistemic feedback loop K_t --Buddhi--> Decision --Action--> W_{t+1} --Omega--> O_{t+1} --Qualify--> K_{t+1}, offered as a strong interpretation of the Gita's Karma/action distinction without claiming the Gita invented the architecture.

rows.anchor: Every valid Kernel operation must preserve KnowledgeOS state integrity. ... I(K_t) => I(K_{t+1}) for every permitted transformation. Provenance preservation: Pi(K_{t+1}) supseteq Pi_required(K_t). Temporal consistency: a later state must not silently erase the fact that an earlier state existed. Identity consistency: an operation must not accidentally create two identities for one object. Relation consistency ... Evidence consistency: a proposition cannot become stronger without an appropriate epistemic basis. This last one is especially important for AI-generated knowledge.
rows.statement: Proposes 'every valid Kernel operation must preserve KnowledgeOS state integrity' as a central research question, requiring discovery of an invariant set I={I_1,...,I_n} with I(K_t) => I(K_{t+1}) for every permitted transformation, exemplified by five candidate invariants: provenance preservation (Pi(K_{t+1}) supseteq Pi_required(K_t)), temporal consistency (a later state must not silently erase that an earlier state existed), identity consistency (no accidental double-identity for one object), relation consistency (a recorded relation must be preserved or explicitly revised), and evidence consistency (a proposition cannot become stronger without appropriate epistemic basis) -- the last flagged as especially important for AI-generated knowledge.
invariants: Pi(K_{t+1}) supseteq Pi_required(K_t)

rows.anchor: STEP 291 -- KNOWLEDGEOS KERNEL OPERATOR DISCOVERY. Strategic Discovery: discover all epistemic transformation families, all state transitions, all primitive transitions, all Buddhi/discrimination functions, all Zero/gap functions, all knowledge-revision functions, all relation transformations, all temporal transformations, all purification candidates, all action/feedback transformations. Tactical Discovery: Input -> Preconditions -> Transformation -> Output -> Evidence -> Provenance -> Invariants. Mathematical Discovery: closure, deterministic, idempotent, compositional, reversible, monotonic. DDD Discovery: Aggregate boundary, Entity, Value Object, Domain Service, Domain Event, invariant, command, decision, policy, lifecycle -- without assuming that every mathematical operator becomes a software method. Gītā Discovery: for every surviving operator ask does the Gītā independently illuminate this operation? Gītā correspondence != KnowledgeOS derivation. Zero Discovery: what can this operation prove that it does not know?
rows.statement: Names and structures the proposed research programme 'STEP 291 -- KNOWLEDGEOS KERNEL OPERATOR DISCOVERY' with six phases: Strategic Discovery (10 categories of transformation families to discover); Tactical Discovery (Input->Preconditions->Transformation->Output->Evidence->Provenance->Invariants per candidate); Mathematical Discovery (closure, determinism, idempotence, compositionality, reversibility, monotonicity); DDD Discovery (Aggregate boundary, Entity, Value Object, Domain Service, Domain Event, invariant, command, decision, policy, lifecycle -- without assuming every operator becomes a software method); Gita Discovery (for every surviving operator, ask whether the Gita independently illuminates it, preserving Gita correspondence != KnowledgeOS derivation); and Zero Discovery (for every operation, ask what it can prove it does not know -- called possibly the deepest part of the entire Kernel).

rows.anchor: the document's proposed Step 291 is directionally right: KnowledgeOS Kernel Operator Discovery. But I would change its mission. Not: Discover the complete operator space. Instead: Construct and audit the candidate operational vocabulary required by the currently ratified KnowledgeOS state model, while proving neither completeness nor canonicality unless independently established. That is much stronger scientifically.

sources.note: Proposes treating Yoga not as literal software translation but as a family of mathematical simulations/operators over the epistemic state: Y:(K_t,O,C,G)->K_{t+1}, with a correspondence table (Dhyana=iterative computation, Dharana=constraint/focus operator, Buddhi=discrimination function, Manas=candidate generation, Indriya=observations, Karma=state-changing operation, Phala=observed consequence, Vairagya=outcome-independent evaluation, Samadhi=convergence/fixed-point condition, Moksha=limiting/boundary condition). Introduces named simulations Yoga-1 (Discrimination, Y_B=B(K,x)), Yoga-2 (Concentration, Y_D=pi_X(K), linked to Step 287 observational equivalence), Yoga-3 (Iterative contemplation/fixed point Y(K*)=K*), and 8 falsification-style test questions per proposed Yoga operator.
The Yoga-as-family-of-mathematical-transformation-regimes framework, first proposed in B0054 and reused/restated in B0055's synthesis (S2263).

rows.anchor: Y:\;(K_t,\mathcal O,\mathcal C,\mathcal G) \longrightarrow K_{t+1}
rows.statement: Yoga modelled as a mathematical simulation/coupling operator Y:(K_t,O,C,G)->K_{t+1} ('a method of bringing different components into an intended relationship or condition'), with correspondence table: Yoga=transformation/coupling operator (simulate state transformation); Dhyana=iterative focused computation (repeated evaluation of one epistemic object); Dharana=constraint/focus operator (restrict computation to relevant dimensions); Buddhi=discrimination function (classify/distinguish alternatives); Manas=fluctuating working process (candidate generation/attention movement); Indriya=input channels (observations); Karma=action/transition (state-changing operation); Phala=resulting state/effect (observed consequence); Vairagya=independence from result (evaluate without outcome-dependent criteria); Samadhi=convergence/stability condition (investigate whether repeated evaluation converges); Moksha=limiting/transcendent condition (whether an epistemic process reaches a defined boundary). Explicitly analytical correspondences, not literal Gita definitions of these mathematical objects.

Three named Yoga simulations: Yoga-1 Discrimination, Y_B(K,x)=B(K,x), testing whether Buddhi can reliably distinguish admissible from inadmissible knowledge; Yoga-2 Concentration, Y_D(K,X)=pi_X(K) (projection onto relevant dimension set X), explicitly resembling the Step 287 result Sigma_1 approx_X Sigma_2 iff pi_X(Sigma_1)=pi_X(Sigma_2) -- focused attention simulated as controlled projection; Yoga-3 Iterative contemplation, K_{t+1}=Y(K_t) iterated as K_0->K_1->K_2->..., asking whether the process reaches a fixed point Y(K*)=K*, giving a rigorous (but non-proving) way to investigate mental stabilization.

rows.anchor: Yoga \neq Knowledge ... K_1=K_2 but Y(K_1)\neq Y(K_2)
rows.statement: Yoga must not be identified with Knowledge or 'more knowledge'; it is a relationship/transformation of epistemic state. Two systems can hold K_1=K_2 while Y(K_1) != Y(K_2), because context, purpose, observations, uncertainty, or operational state differs -- connecting to the Step 287 distinction between structural, semantic and observational equality. Also proposes making Yoga explicitly temporal: K_{t+1}=Y_t(K_t,O_t,C_t), noting dK/dt may not be meaningful as a continuous derivative since KnowledgeOS state may be discrete/event-driven, so K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,o_t) is preferred, with Yoga as a family of possible transition strategies over delta.

rows.anchor: B(x)= \begin{cases}\text{admissible}\\\text{inadmissible}\\\text{unknown}\\\text{conflicting}\\\text{requires qualification}\end{cases}
rows.statement: Buddhi modelled as B: E -> D (epistemic alternatives to distinguishable outcomes) with candidate codomain {admissible, inadmissible, unknown, conflicting, requires qualification}; the 'requires qualification' category connects directly to the unresolved Qualify/G1 problem.

rows.anchor: Does the operator type-check? ... Does it merely provide philosophical interpretation?
rows.statement: Reframes the research question from 'What does Yoga mean in KnowledgeOS?' to 'Which mathematically definable transformations of epistemic state can be interpreted through Yoga, and which are independently required by KnowledgeOS?'. Proposes an 8-question falsification protocol per proposed Yoga operator: (1) does it type-check, (2) does KnowledgeOS independently require it, (3) does it operate on existing primitives, (4) does it introduce a new primitive, (5) can it be falsified, (6) does it produce a useful simulation, (7) does it change the Kernel model, (8) does it merely provide philosophical interpretation. Proposes next step: construct a Yoga Operator Algebra (Y_B, Y_D, Y_R, Y_C, ...) tested against K_t, Sigma, delta, Zero, Qualify, A, R. Records provisional (non-canonical) positions: Yoga ~ family of epistemic-state transformation simulations; Buddhi ~ discrimination/evaluation operator; Mind ~ philosophical lens for analysing Kernel behaviour.

rows.anchor: Policy: Context\times Action \rightarrow \{Must,May,MustNot,Conditional\}. Policy is therefore not evidence. It is not authority. It is not a decision. It constrains decisions/actions.
rows.statement: Canonical definition of Policy ('what normative constraints govern behavior in this context?') as a function Context x Action -> {Must,May,MustNot,Conditional}, explicitly distinct from evidence, authority, and decision -- it constrains decisions/actions rather than being one.

rows.anchor: Policy\neq Authority. Policy answers: What may/should be done? while: Authority answers: Who may legitimately decide or perform it?
rows.statement: Separates Policy (what may/should be done) from Authority (who may legitimately decide/perform it) as a crucial, previously-missing distinction.

rows.statement: New invariant I_74: a decision or action must be evaluated against applicable policy before being considered governance-valid, subject to an explicit exception mechanism.

rows.statement: Formalizes exception handling: a PolicyViolation can become an ExceptionGranted state via an authorized actor satisfying an exception policy, but the exception never deletes or overwrites the original policy -- Exception != PolicyDeletion.

sources.note: A three-layer architecture (distinct in shape from the eight-bounded-context map): Epistemic Kernel (Claim, Evidence, Basing, Provenance, Epistemic Standing, Input/Transition Rules, Inference, Reliability relation, Revision, Challenge, Temporal identity); Epistemic Mechanisms (Deduction, Induction, Bayesian methods, Search, Perception, Memory, LLM reasoning, Retrieval, Simulation, Testing, Statistical inference); Institutional/Operational (Governance, Authority, Risk, Decision, Human review, Regulatory policy, Workflow, Agent orchestration, Organizational roles).

rows.anchor: Otto stores information in a notebook and consults it functionally like another person's biological memory. ... the specific process matters. ... Extended Mind should NOT become a Kernel entity. The Kernel should say: epistemically relevant processes may cross system boundaries.
rows.statement: Clark & Chalmers' Otto/Notebook extended-mind example supports the principle that epistemically relevant processes may cross system boundaries (human cognition, tool-assisted cognition, external artifact, environment), but Extended Mind itself must not become a Kernel entity -- only the principle is promoted, concrete tools (Notebook/Git/IDE/Database/LLM/Calculator/search engine/CI) stay outside.

rows.anchor: If premises are true and the inference is valid ... but the conclusion cannot add information beyond the premises. ... Induction: the conclusion can extend beyond the premises, but only probabilistically. ... DeductiveInference, InductiveInference should be distinct mechanism types.
rows.statement: Deduction (no information beyond premises) vs Induction (extends beyond premises probabilistically) should remain distinct mechanism types under one Inference vocabulary (Deductive/Inductive/Abductive-candidate/Probabilistic/Other) with only Inference/InferenceType/Validity-Support in the Kernel, algorithms outside.

rows.anchor: KNOW-HOW, KNOWLEDGE-WH, KNOWLEDGE-THAT ... some procedural know-how is not simply propositional knowledge. ... a Kernel vocabulary distinction, with the concrete models outside Kernel until DDD scenarios prove ownership.
rows.statement: KnowledgeObject vocabulary distinction (Proposition / Procedure-Know-how / Entity-Referential knowledge) kept as vocabulary only, not yet promoted to separate Kernel aggregates, pending DDD scenario proof of ownership.

rows.anchor: EPISTEMIC KERNEL / EPISTEMIC MECHANISMS / INSTITUTIONAL-OPERATIONAL ... This book strongly supports this separation. ... The Kernel should know that a process occurred and what epistemic role it played, not how every process is implemented.
rows.statement: Full three-layer architecture with explicit membership lists for each layer, and the governing rule that the Kernel records that a process occurred and its epistemic role, never how the process is implemented.

rows.anchor: the Kernel should govern epistemic relationships, not epistemic algorithms ... it should not answer: Should Bayesian inference be used? ... Which decision threshold should the business use? ... The KnowledgeOS Kernel is not a database of knowledge and not a truth engine.
rows.statement: Deepest finding: the Kernel should answer what-is-a-claim/what-counts-as-evidence/what-is-basing/what-transformations/what-is-provenance/what-is-standing questions, never algorithm-choice or threshold questions; final Kernel formulation is a governed epistemic substrate preserving claims/evidence/basing/provenance/epistemic processes/admissible inputs/admissible transitions/reliability conditions/assessments/challenges/revisions, with everything else (LLMs, Bayesian inference, search, memory stores, RAG, tests, agents, reviewers, statistical methods, workflows, decision policies) operating on top without becoming the substrate.

sources.note: Research hypothesis (Evidence-Gated Hybrid Temporal Inference) proposing KnowledgeOS use a coarse-to-fine inference ladder (Rules -> HMM -> HSMM -> Deep Bayesian/temporal inference -> Human/Governance) rather than one universal model, with lenses (DDD/Zero/Nyaya/etc.) acting as complexity-reduction and escalation-trigger mechanisms; HMM is treated as a special case of HSMM (geometric duration), used as the cheap default, escalating to HSMM only for states with demonstrably non-geometric duration, and to deep/human review only when risk justifies the cost.

rows.anchor: Use the cheapest lens/model that can answer the current question with sufficient accuracy, and escalate only when the evidence shows that the cheap model is inadequate. ... coarse-to-fine, evidence-gated, hybrid temporal inference architecture.
rows.statement: Core hybrid-architecture thesis: Deterministic Core + Fast Probabilistic Model (HMM) + Selective HSMM + Deep Offline Inference, rather than making HSMM the universal substrate; explicit pipeline Normalize/Filter -> Deterministic Gate -> {Fast Model | HSMM Model} -> Assurance Gate -> {Accept | Deep Inference/Review}.

rows.anchor: the lenses themselves become a complexity-reduction mechanism. ... DDD reduces the mathematical state space ... Reducing M from 100 to 10 gives a theoretical transition-space reduction of roughly 100 (before even optimizing duration).
rows.statement: Reframes the corpus's existing philosophical lenses (DDD/Zero/Vani/Panini/Karaka/Nyaya/Navya-Nyaya/Godel/Escher/Siva-Sakti/Ganesha/Leonardo/Moksha/Negative-Epistemology/Isnad/Witness/Dharma/Wisdom) as a table of computational roles (state-space reduction, missing-prerequisite detection, normalization, feature extraction, justification validation, truth-collapse prevention, invariant preservation, admission gating, context completeness, staleness detection, forbidden-inference-path rejection, provenance quality, escalation decision) -- DDD's bounded-context state reduction alone is quantified as roughly two orders of magnitude before duration modelling is even considered.

rows.anchor: if prerequisite == absent: return INSUFFICIENT_BASIS. This is O(1) or close to linear validation cost, instead of O(TM^2D). ... Zero becomes the first optimization gate.
rows.statement: Zero Lens becomes the first computational optimization gate: absence of a constitutive prerequisite (identity/context/evidence/justification/candidate/agreement) short-circuits to INSUFFICIENT_BASIS at near-constant cost, avoiding expensive HSMM computation entirely for cases that fail this cheap check.

rows.anchor: For each state s, estimate D_s^observed and compare it with the geometric duration implied by the HMM. If KL(...) < epsilon then HMM is probably adequate. ... Only Proposed, Assured, Operational have highly non-geometric durations. Then use: Hybrid: HMM states + explicit-duration states.
rows.statement: Empirical HSMM-activation criterion via KL divergence between observed and geometric-implied state-duration distributions; state-specific hybrid model where only some states (e.g. Proposed/Assured/Operational) get explicit-duration HSMM treatment and others keep the cheaper geometric HMM assumption, reducing computation versus applying HSMM to the whole state space.

rows.anchor: Once SNF(x)=s we cache x -> s. ... CacheKey = (SemanticHash, Context, ModelVersion, EvidenceClass). ... This prevents invalid cross-context reuse.
rows.statement: Semantic-normal-form caching optimization (reuse prior inference for semantically equivalent observations) refined by a provenance-aware CacheKey (semantic hash, context, model version, evidence class) so semantically identical but differently-provenanced observations are not invalidly conflated.

rows.anchor: Inference = Gate_{DDD,Zero,Nyaya} o Normalize_{Vani,Panini,SNF} o Select[Deterministic, HMM, HSMM, Deep] ... final acceptance constrained by: Truth != Inference != Evidence != Authority. ... KnowledgeOS becomes an adaptive epistemic computation system ... inference ladder.
rows.statement: Final compressed formula for the whole hybrid architecture (Gate then Normalize then Select among Deterministic/HMM/HSMM/Deep) bounded by Truth!=Inference!=Evidence!=Authority; the genuinely novel claim is not 'use HSMM' but that KnowledgeOS becomes an adaptive epistemic computation system with an inference ladder (Rules->HMM->HSMM->Deep->Human/Governance) where lenses determine when and why the system climbs it, frozen as the research hypothesis Evidence-Gated Hybrid Temporal Inference (EG-HTI) with four defining properties.

sources.note: HPA per-chapter analysis mapping Gita Ch17 (Shraddha Traya Vibhag Yoga) threefold faith/food/sacrifice/austerity/charity qualities (Sattva/Rajas/Tamas) onto a KnowledgeOS 'quality classification and trust' theory: Quality(X) in {Sattva,Rajas,Tamas}, Trust(K_t)=Faith(K_t), Outcome(K_t)=Trust(K_t)*Action(K_t).

rows.anchor: Faith (Shraddha) is not blind belief. It is epistemic trust that varies by quality (Sattva, Rajas, Tamas). The quality of faith determines the quality of knowledge, action, and outcome.
rows.statement: Thesis: faith/trust is not binary but has three qualities (Sattva/Rajas/Tamas) which determine the quality of downstream knowledge, action and outcome; framed as the 'missing quality assurance and trust verification layer' of KnowledgeOS.

rows.anchor: Quality(Evidence) ∈ {Sattva, Rajas, Tamas} ... Quality(Assessment) ∈ {Sattva, Rajas, Tamas} ... Quality(Discipline) ∈ {Sattva, Rajas, Tamas} ... Quality(KnowledgeSharing) ∈ {Sattva, Rajas, Tamas}
rows.statement: Applies a uniform three-valued quality classification (Sattva=high-quality/unbiased/selfless, Rajas=emotionally-charged/self-serving/status-driven, Tamas=low-quality/biased/harmful) across four distinct KnowledgeOS dimensions: evidence, assessment, discipline, and knowledge-sharing — each treated as an instance of the same generic Quality(X) function.

rows.anchor: Classify(X) = Sattva if Integrity(X) > Passion(X) + Ignorance(X); Rajas if Passion(X) > Integrity(X) + Ignorance(X); Tamas if Ignorance(X) > Integrity(X) + Passion(X)
rows.statement: Proposes a comparative classification rule for the three-valued quality (pairwise-majority style: whichever of Integrity/Passion/Ignorance strictly dominates the sum of the other two) with no stated measurement procedure, units, or normalization for the three component quantities.
missing: measurement procedure for Integrity/Passion/Ignorance
tie-breaking when no term dominates

rows.anchor: Trust(K_t) = Faith_Sattva(K_t) - Faith_Rajas(K_t) - Faith_Tamas(K_t) ... Trust(K_t) > 0 ⟺ System is Sattvic
rows.statement: Defines a scalar Trust(K_t) as the difference between a system's Sattvic faith component and the sum of its Rajasic and Tamasic components, with positive Trust equated to the system being classified 'Sattvic'.

sources.note: A proposed five-way classification for every remaining open item in a theory-closure effort: A Theory-critical (if unresolved, the meaning of the theory is undefined), B Theory-parameterized (the theory deliberately allows multiple valid implementations/semantics), C Implementation obligation (the theory is defined but implementation must demonstrate it), D Empirical obligation (theory defined, real-world evidence still required), E Governance obligation (theory cannot decide it; governance must). Closure criterion: Theory Closed iff no unresolved A-items remain. Proposed to replace repeated ad hoc C1-C4-style closure attempts with a single classificatory gate artifact THEORY-CLOSURE-GATE-2026-v1.0.

rows.anchor: My recommendation: one final closure gate ... THEORY-CLOSURE-GATE-2026-v1.0. Its purpose is not to invent anything. For every remaining item, classify: A Theory-critical ... B Theory-parameterized ... C Implementation obligation ... D Empirical obligation ... E Governance obligation ... Theory Closed iff No unresolved A-items remain.
rows.statement: Proposes a single final artifact THEORY-CLOSURE-GATE-2026-v1.0 that classifies every remaining open item into one of five categories (A Theory-critical, B Theory-parameterized-by-design, C Implementation obligation, D Empirical obligation, E Governance obligation) and defines theory closure as: Theory Closed iff no unresolved A-items remain -- explicitly recommending this replace another cycle of C1-C4-style closure attempts.
