sources.note: Rereads Gita Chapter 4 (Jnana Yoga, doubt destroyed by knowledge) against the completed Chapters 5-18 model, adding the missing layer of how the kernel transforms knowledge and resolves doubt. Proposes the pipeline Ajnana(ignorance)->Samsaya(doubt)->Jnana(investigation/knowledge)->Buddhi(discrimination)->Karma(action), models Jnana as a TRANSFORMATION OPERATOR J:(K_t,Doubt_t)->(K_{t+1},Doubt_{t+1}) with intended Doubt_{t+1}<Doubt_t (not merely a primitive/object), and explicitly separates Zero (missing/absent knowledge) from Samsaya/doubt (unresolved uncertainty between conflicting claims) in a five-row table (Zero/Samsaya/Ajnana/Jnana/Buddhi). Proposes a five-component knowledge state K_t=(X_t,Sigma_t,Pi_t,Gamma_t,Delta_t) [content, epistemic quality, provenance, context, detected gaps]. Poses four distinct candidate readings of K_1 equiv K_2 (content equality, epistemic equality, provenance-sensitive cong_lambda, behavioural equality via delta) as motivated but NOT solved by Chapter 4, explicitly preserving Step 287's OPEN status. Gives Knowledge != Action but Knowledge -> better-qualified action, reinforcing Command != Transformation. Proposes a five-operator formal algebra Omega(observe),Q(qualify),J(know/transform),B(discriminate),A(act) with explicit composition K_{t+1}=J(Q(Omega(W_t)),K_t), D_t=B(K_{t+1},C_t), W_{t+1}=A(D_t,W_t). Closes by proposing to freeze a KERNEL-CANDIDATE-v1={K_t,Zero,Samsaya,Jnana,Buddhi,Decision,Action} and mathematically test operators J,B,A,Omega,Q for closure/typing/identity/composition/reversibility/monotonicity/information-loss before continuing to add Gita terminology.

rows.anchor: Jñāna : (K_t,\;Doubt_t) \rightarrow (K_{t+1},\;Doubt_{t+1})
rows.statement: From the closing verses (knowledge as a weapon that cuts doubt arising from ignorance): models Jnana not as a primitive/object but as a transformation operator J:(K_t,Doubt_t)->(K_{t+1},Doubt_{t+1}), with intended effect Doubt_{t+1}<Doubt_t under appropriate conditions -- reinforcing the earlier Jnana~delta interpretation over Jnana=Knowledge. Also formalizes Ajnana->Samsaya->Jnana->Buddhi->Karma as a candidate kernel cycle: ignorance->doubt->investigation->knowledge->discrimination->decision->action->new observation->updated K_t.

lineage_claims.quote: Chapter 4 strengthens that interpretation.

rows.anchor: Zero \neq Doubt ... "I don't know X." -> Zero ... "I have two conflicting claims about X." -> Samsaya
rows.statement: Explicitly separates five concepts previously at risk of conflation: Zero (detection of missing/absent knowledge, 'I don't know X'); Samsaya/doubt (unresolved epistemic uncertainty, 'I have two conflicting claims about X'); Ajnana (lack/absence of understanding); Jnana (knowledge/transformation that resolves or transforms uncertainty, 'evidence establishes claim A'); Buddhi (discrimination/decision capability, 'therefore accept A'). Zero != Doubt is proposed as an excellent candidate for formalization.
invariants: Zero != Samsaya (doubt)

rows.anchor: K_t=(X_t,\Sigma_t,\Pi_t,\Gamma_t,\Delta_t)
rows.statement: Proposes KnowledgeOS is not fundamentally a set (beyond K_t subset K): a five-component knowledge state K_t=(X_t,Sigma_t,Pi_t,Gamma_t,Delta_t) where X_t=represented knowledge content, Sigma_t=epistemic quality/state dimensions, Pi_t=provenance, Gamma_t=context/constraints, Delta_t=detected gaps/uncertainties, with kernel transitions K_{t+1}=F(K_t,O_t,B_t,A_t) -- assessed as a much richer mathematical object than K_t subset K alone.

rows.anchor: Content equality? ... Epistemic equality? ... Provenance-sensitive equality? ... Behavioural equality?
rows.statement: Explicitly connects Chapter 4's doubt/knowledge/lineage material to the Step 287 open equality problem K_1 equiv K_2, posing four distinct candidate readings: content equality (X_1=X_2); epistemic equality (Sigma_1=Sigma_2); provenance-sensitive equality ((X_1,Pi_1) cong_lambda (X_2,Pi_2)); behavioural equality (delta(K_1,o)=delta(K_2,o) for all o). States plainly that Chapter 4 gives philosophical motivation for asking this question but does not provide the mathematical answer -- Step 287's OPEN status remains correct.
missing: resolution of which equality notion is canonical

rows.statement: Constructs a five-operator formal algebra: Omega:W->O (observe), Q:O->E (qualify), J:ExK->K' (know/transform), B:K'xC->D (discriminate), A:D->W' (act), with explicit composition K_{t+1}=J(Q(Omega(W_t)),K_t), D_t=B(K_{t+1},C_t), W_{t+1}=A(D_t,W_t). Proposes working kernel definition Kernel=(K_t,Omega,Q,J,B,A,Delta,Sigma,Pi) with central transition K_t --Omega,Q--> E_t --J--> K'_t --B--> D_t --A--> W_{t+1} --Omega--> K_{t+1}, explicitly non-canonical pending formal validation. Frames Chapter 4's strongest contribution as a theory of what the kernel DOES with knowledge (Knowledge->discrimination->decision->action->new state), not another primitive.

rows.statement: Recommends, before simulating the whole Gita-KnowledgeOS system, freezing a minimal KERNEL-CANDIDATE-v1 = {K_t, Zero, Samsaya, Jnana, Buddhi, Decision, Action} and mathematically testing operators J, B, A, Omega, Q for closure, typing, identity, composition, reversibility, monotonicity, and information loss -- explicit caution that the source's religious claims must not be converted into technical claims by analogy alone; the strongest candidates are those independently derivable from KnowledgeOS per Step 286. Chapter 4 generates and corroborates hypotheses; it does not ratify the kernel.

sources.note: A DeepSeek external-research artifact (phase_measure_theory/external_research/) systematically mapping the chapters of a GPT-style LLM-from-scratch technical book (tokenization, attention, training loop, pretrained-weight loading, data pipelines, evaluation, fine-tuning, instruction tuning) onto proposed KnowledgeOS implementation components, with worked code adaptations, three explicit anti-import warnings (no objective-truth assumption, no end-to-end single-model training, no single-model architecture), and a summary mapping table plus six next steps; unvetted per the folder readme, wholly new to the indexed corpus.

rows.anchor:
Book: Raw Text -> Tokenization -> Token IDs -> Embeddings
KnowledgeOS: Source Observation -> Semantic Interpretation -> Candidate Assertion
... The tokenization pipeline is exactly what we need for the Source Observation layer.
rows.statement: Proposes reusing a BPE tokenization pipeline (via tiktoken) directly as the Source Observation layer's text-ingestion mechanism, converting raw text into token IDs before any further semantic processing, while explicitly noting the full embedding pipeline is not needed unless an LLM is used for interpretation.

rows.anchor:
Book: Attention weights determine token importance
KnowledgeOS: Evidence weights determine assertion importance ... The book's attention is about tokens within a sequence. Our evidence attention is about evidence items within a set. The mathematical structure is similar but the semantics differ.
rows.statement: Proposes adapting scaled dot-product / multi-head attention (query=proposition being assessed, key=each evidence's relevance, value=each evidence's weight) into an "EvidenceAttention" mechanism for aggregating evidence importance, while noting explicitly the mathematical structure is analogous but the semantics of the input set (evidence items, not sequence tokens) differ.

type_signature.domain: evidence set given a proposition query

missing: definition of what evidence relevance/weight numerically represents

rows.anchor:
while not decision_ready:
    observation = observe(source)
    interpretation = interpret(observation)
    candidate = construct_assertion(interpretation)
    evidence = assess_evidence(candidate)
    assertion = admit(candidate, evidence)
    knowledge = update_knowledge(assertion)
    zero = detect_gaps(knowledge)
    lord = generate_candidates(knowledge, zero)
    sarathi = recommend_action(knowledge, lord)
rows.statement: Proposes an "epistemic loop" pseudocode -- observe, interpret, construct_assertion, assess_evidence, admit, update_knowledge, detect_gaps (Zero), generate_candidates (Lord), recommend_action (Sarathi), repeating until decision_ready -- explicitly analogized to (but conceptually distinct from) the book's per-epoch training loop that updates model weights; the book's loop optimizes weights, this loop optimizes knowledge state, but the iterate-evaluate-update pattern is claimed directly transferable.
missing: termination/convergence criterion for decision_ready

rows.anchor: Book's assumption: The model learns to predict the "correct" next token. There is an objective truth in the training data. KnowledgeOS's principle: There is no objective truth. Knowledge is always provisional, epistemic, and context-dependent. What to avoid: Don't assume the LLM's output is "true." Always treat it as a candidate interpretation.
rows.statement: Warns explicitly against importing the source book's implicit "objective truth in training data" assumption into KnowledgeOS: KnowledgeOS's principle is that there is no objective truth and knowledge is always provisional/epistemic/context-dependent, so any LLM output must always be treated as a candidate interpretation, never as true.
invariants: LLM output is always a candidate interpretation, never asserted truth

rows.anchor: Book: One model (GPT) handles everything from tokenization to generation. KnowledgeOS: Multiple components (Source Processing, Interpretation, Knowledge State, Zero, Lord, Sarathi) with distinct responsibilities. What to adapt: The book's GPT model becomes one component (the Cognitive Layer) within KnowledgeOS, not the entire system.
rows.statement: Warns against adopting the book's single end-to-end model architecture: KnowledgeOS must remain a composition of distinct-responsibility components (Source Processing, Interpretation, Knowledge State, Zero, Lord, Sarathi), with any LLM (like the book's GPT model) demoted to a single component (the Cognitive Layer) rather than treated as the entire system.

sources.note: Step 288's level-discipline and completeness-matrix artifact: pins every equality-family relation to one of ten levels (L-value through L-system/behaviour), audits fifteen candidate level-promotions (10 invalid, 2 valid-as-theorem, 3 unproven), re-confirms the Sigma-order != K-order separation is clean across the whole programme, distinguishes 'decidable' from 'always returns a decision', and produces a ten-relation x eight-column completeness matrix concluding zero unconditional Level-5 state relations, zero proven congruences, and empty implementable/governance-authorized columns throughout.

rows.anchor: ## §3.4 The reconciled matrix (mandate §3 columns) ... $$\boxed{\text{ZERO unconditional Level-5 state-level relations...}}$$
rows.statement: Produces a full reconciliation matrix across all mandate-required columns (level, corpus definition, source, decision procedure, computability, equivalence properties, congruence, provenance/governance inclusion, identity involvement, dependencies, contradictions, normative decisions) for eight named relations (=, ≡, ≈, ≅_λ/≅_P, ≅_I, ≅_H/∼_H/≡_𝒯, Continuity, ≡_D). Key entries: '=' is computable only relative to canonicalization and is NOT a congruence (executed); '≡' is not fully decidable and has transitivity unestablished; '≈' has no decision procedure since its observation set 𝒪_K is not closed; ≅_I is an equivalence relation only within a context (I_48); ≡_D is the only relation fully specified but sits at the wrong (value) level for K.

rows.anchor: | Level | Relations resident at this level | ... **L-operation** | — 🔴 **no relation defined; `𝒪` unratified** | **L-event** | — 🔴 **no schema** | **L-policy** | — 🔴 |
rows.statement: Pins every named equality-family relation to exactly one of ten mandate-required levels: L-value (≡_D); L-assertion (≡_exact, ≡_struct, ≡_sem,C, refinement ⪯, the seven 25J.26 edges); L-entity/object (=_I,=_V,=_S,=_E, ≅_I, EntityID/KAID/RecordID); L-state (=,≡,≈,≅_λ/≅_P); L-history (∼_H,≅_H,≡_𝒯,∼_F); L-provenance (Pi identity, ≅_P); L-system/behaviour (∼_H under all sigma, Continuity); while L-operation, L-event, and L-policy have NO relation defined at all (operation registry 𝒪 unratified; no event schema; nothing at the policy level), and L-observation's 𝒪_K is explicitly not closed.
missing: relations at L-operation, L-event, L-policy

rows.anchor: ## §4b Promotion audit — SOURCE LEVEL → TARGET LEVEL ... $$\boxed{\text{ZERO unconditional Level-5 state-level relations. ZERO proven congruences. Implementable: empty. Governance-authorized: empty.}}$$
rows.statement: Audits fifteen specific candidate level-promotions, finding ten INVALID (e.g. value-level equiv_D to state-level equiv; Sigma structural equality to K structural equality; Sigma order to K order -- the 'F5 error'; approx_X to corpus's approx; finite-sample agreement to equality, executed; hash equality to semantic equality, executed; decidability to congruence, executed; fold equality to behavioural equality; context-scoped cong_I transitivity to global transitivity; similarity threshold to identity), two VALID as proven theorems (X subset Y implies approx_Y refines approx_X, executed; approx_X is an equivalence relation for every X, executed), and three UNPROVEN (corpus's approx is an equivalence relation, blocked because 𝒪_K is not closed so there is no function to take the kernel of; equiv_sem is transitive; any equiv-implies-approx hierarchy, which is additionally forbidden as a chain per 261.9/258.19). Concludes zero unconditional Level-5 state-level relations, zero proven congruences, and empty implementable/governance-authorized columns across the whole family.

rows.anchor: ## §15 THE RESULT DOMAIN — "decidable" vs "always returns a decision" ... $$\boxed{\text{A procedure that answers } Unknown \text{ is NOT a complete equality decision procedure.}}$$
rows.statement: Restates the four rival result-domain codomains (25S.3, 38.10, 012 §35, 012 §36/46) and the Relation-vs-Status sorting principle (012 §36), applying the mandate's own distinction between 'decidable relation' (a total procedure that returns TRUE/FALSE correctly) and 'procedure that always returns a decision' (a total procedure may legitimately answer Unknown without deciding); boxes the resulting principle that an Unknown-returning procedure is NOT a complete equality decision procedure, and reiterates 012 §35's theorem-shaped result that semantic equality can never reach a total Boolean procedure, agreeing with three other independent loci (224.11, 25S.4, 38.22) that this is a feature, not a failure.
invariants: a procedure that answers Unknown is not a complete equality decision procedure

rows.anchor: ## The completeness matrix — TWO orthogonal axes ... A relation can be maximally decidable and semantically useless — `=` is exactly that.
rows.statement: Produces a ten-relation completeness matrix (=, ≡, ≈, ≅_P, ≅_I, ≅_H/≡_𝒯, ∼_F fold, Continuity, ≡_D, and the author's own ≈_X) across eight columns (Named/Defined/Typed/Parameterized/Decidable/Implementable/Governance-authorized/Congruent), explicitly separating procedure strength from semantic soundness (congruence) as two orthogonal axes -- observing a relation can be maximally decidable and semantically useless, and '=' is exactly that example (fully named/defined/typed but only conditionally decidable and proven NOT a congruence). Result: implementable and governance-authorized columns are empty across all ten relations; zero proven congruences anywhere in the matrix.

rows.anchor: a finding is M (mechanical) if a deterministic checker over the artifact could have produced it with no architectural judgement... 29 % → 46 % → 58 %
rows.statement: Classifying every new finding across the AMD3/AMD4/AMD5 independent reviews as mechanical (M) or judgement (J) shows the mechanical share rose from 29% (4/14) to 46% (6/13) to 58% (7/12) as the migration-plan design stabilised — a measured trend across three independent reviewers, none of whom was looking for it, showing an increasing share of scarce independent-architecture review capacity was spent on machine-catchable defects.

rows.anchor: The cost is not reviewer minutes — it is AMENDMENT CYCLES ... a mechanical defect found by an independent reviewer does not cost a review. It costs a whole amendment plus a whole re-review.
rows.statement: Reframes the cost model: a mechanical defect caught late costs a full amendment cycle plus a full re-review, not merely reviewer minutes; measures the concrete chain volume (4,315 lines of governed artifact, 5 amendment commits, 4 independent reviews, 12 registered commission corrections) for a migration that had, at that point, not executed a single line of implementation.

rows.anchor: Automation may reduce the COST of assurance and must never manufacture AUTHORITY.
rows.statement: Proposes a candidate invariant governing all future assurance automation: automation may reduce the cost of assurance work but must never manufacture authority, stated as the machine-facing case of the estate's existing G-2/R5b rule ('a grant registers a human act by reference — the record never manufactures authority'); explicitly marked a candidate from one track's evidence, not yet promoted.
invariants: Automation may reduce the COST of assurance and must never manufacture AUTHORITY.

rows.anchor: X-5 ... a checker reduces dangling-reference defects to zero and reduces missing-act defects (RD-1, RD-7, RD-3·b) by NOTHING. Only a human notices an act the author never declared.
rows.statement: Corrects the proposal's over-claim about the automatability of a four-layer trace: VERIFYING that a declared trace's identifiers all resolve is deterministic and would have caught prior dangling-reference defects, but DERIVING the act list in the first place (noticing that an act was never declared at all) is judgement and is not touched by any checker; the biggest correction the review makes is refusing to conflate the two.

sources.note: Step 164's provisional candidate event catalog organized into four categories -- epistemic events (EvidenceCaptured, EvidenceValidated, KnowledgeProposed, KnowledgeConfirmed, KnowledgeContested, KnowledgeSuperseded, DeterminationProposed, DeterminationEstablished), governance events (DecisionProposed, DecisionMade, DecisionDeferred, DecisionEscalated, DispositionRefrain), authorization events (AuthorizationRequested, AuthorizationGranted, AuthorizationDenied, AuthorizationExpired), operational events (ActionCreated, ActionExecuted, ExecutionFailed, ExecutionOutcomeObserved) -- with per-event invariant qualifications (e.g. EvidenceCaptured establishes existence not validity; EvidenceValidated!=True; KnowledgeConfirmed requires ConfirmationCriteriaSatisfied; DecisionMade does not imply AuthorizationGranted; AuthorizationGranted does not imply Execution; ActionCreated!=ActionExecuted) and an explicit non-mandatory branching event graph (e.g. DeterminationProposed can branch to Rejected/Deferred/Escalated/Accepted). Includes CandidateDetermination!=EstablishedDetermination as 'the epistemic equivalent of a pull request awaiting review', and DispositionRefrain (a deliberate decision not to act) as a valid, auditable, intentional outcome, not failure.

rows.anchor: EvidenceCaptured ⇏ EvidenceValid. ... Validated ≠ True. ... RejectedEvidence ≠ FalseObservation. ... KnowledgeProposed does not mean: KnowledgeConfirmed. ... KnowledgeConfirmed ⇒ ConfirmationCriteriaSatisfied. ... CandidateDetermination ≠ EstablishedDetermination. This is the epistemic equivalent of a pull request awaiting review. ... DecisionMade ⇏ AuthorizationGranted. ... AuthorizationGranted ⇏ Execution. ... ActionCreated ≠ ActionExecuted.
rows.statement: Chains together per-event non-implication invariants across the pipeline: EvidenceCaptured does not imply EvidenceValid; EvidenceValidated!=True (validation establishes procedure-satisfaction, not truth); EvidenceRejected != FalseObservation (rejection may mean unsuitable for this context, not that the underlying observation is false); KnowledgeProposed does not imply KnowledgeConfirmed; KnowledgeConfirmed requires ConfirmationCriteriaSatisfied per applicable context/policy; CandidateDetermination != EstablishedDetermination ('the epistemic equivalent of a pull request awaiting review'); DecisionMade does not imply AuthorizationGranted; AuthorizationGranted does not imply Execution; ActionCreated != ActionExecuted. Also: contradictory knowledge produces KnowledgeContested rather than silent replacement, and a later-authoritative claim produces KnowledgeSuperseded with supersededBy=K2 while K1's historical existence remains.

rows.anchor: DecisionDeferred. The meaning is: No operational decision has yet been authorized. This is not failure. ... DecisionEscalated. ... Escalation ≠ Failure. ... DecisionDispositionSetToRefrain. This represents a deliberate decision not to act. ... Input → Determine → DoNothing. The 'do nothing' outcome must be intentional and auditable.
rows.statement: Elaborates the ActionDisposition branch events at the domain-event level: DecisionDeferred means no operational decision has yet been authorized (not failure); DecisionEscalated means authority was insufficient or the case needs higher governance (Escalation != Failure); DecisionDispositionSetToRefrain represents a deliberate, intentional and auditable decision not to act (KnowledgeOS should support Input -> Determine -> DoNothing as a valid outcome, unlike conventional workflows that implicitly assume Input -> Action).

rows.anchor: ObservedResult = ∅. But: TrueResult ∈ {Success,Failure}. Therefore: ObservedResult missing ⇏ TrueResult = Failure. This is exactly the same epistemic principle we established earlier: Unknown ≠ False. ... It would be dangerous to automatically record: Failure.
rows.statement: Reframes an unconfirmed execution result (e.g. a command issued but connection lost before confirmation, ExecutionStatus=UNKNOWN) as a missing-data statistical problem: ObservedResult=empty does not imply TrueResult=Failure, restating Unknown!=False in the execution-outcome context and warning it would be dangerous to auto-record Failure for a merely unconfirmed result.
invariants: ObservedResult-missing does not imply TrueResult=Failure

rows.anchor: Past events should not be rewritten merely because our interpretation changed. If our interpretation changes, we record a new event. ... Correction from Erasure. ... A historical fact should not be silently rewritten. ... Correlation ≠ Causation. ... we should not automatically claim: E1 ⇒ D1 unless the Determination explicitly identifies E1 as an input. Thus causal lineage should be explicit.
rows.statement: Event immutability invariant: past events must not be rewritten merely because interpretation later changes (a re-interpretation is recorded as a new event, e.g. K1 Confirmed then later K1 Contested, without erasing the earlier confirmation); distinguishes Correction from Erasure (mechanism depends on legal/governance requirements, but semantically a historical fact should not be silently rewritten). Distinguishes Correlation (events belonging to the same case/process, via CorrelationID) from Causation (one event directly contributed to another, via an explicit causation graph Event_i --caused/contributed--> Event_j) -- shared correlation must never be treated as implying causation unless a Determination explicitly cites the earlier event as an input. Proposes an event envelope schema {EventID, EventType, AggregateID, Context, Timestamp, Actor, Authority, CorrelationID, CausationID, Payload} as a semantic contract, not yet a database schema, with AggregateID needed so an event unambiguously affects exactly one owning aggregate.

sources.note: A proposal modelling the Ideal State as a field of positive (+n, supporting) and negative (-n, opposing) numerically-weighted arguments whose reconciliation (summing to zero) constitutes knowledge/fact, with Fact defined as the infinite-time limit of the knowledge-reconciliation process, elaborated with a full argument algebra (combine/subtract/weight operators) and re-cast through the sexual-yoni metaphor as persons/prosecutor-defender/judge generating and reconciling arguments.

rows.anchor: Knowledge = Ideal State = 0. Not because there is no knowledge, but because all arguments are reconciled. ... Fact = lim_{t->infinity} Knowledge_t
rows.statement: Proposes Knowledge/Ideal-State as numeric zero, meaning full reconciliation of positive and negative weighted arguments, and Fact as the infinite-time limit of the reconciliation process.

rows.anchor: Net = sum_i w_i * sign_i ... Net > 0 | Arguments in favor dominate ... Reconcile: Arguments -> Knowledge ... this function takes all arguments (+ and -), weighs them, and produces a knowledge state.
rows.statement: Defines a weighted-sum argument algebra (positive/negative arguments each with a weight and sign) and a Reconcile function mapping the argument set to a knowledge state via net sign.

rows.anchor: Person A = seed ... Person B = womb ... New Knowledge = Person A x Person B ... The Orgasm of Reconciliation: the moment of reconciliation -- when all arguments are resolved -- is the orgasm of knowledge.
rows.statement: Re-expresses the argument-reconciliation model through the sexual-yoni metaphor (positive/negative arguments as penetration/withdrawal, reconciliation as orgasm, resulting knowledge as offspring).

rows.anchor: Fact = lim_{t->infinity} K_t ... this is not justified mathematically or epistemically ... Even if it exists, it need not equal truth.
rows.statement: Rejects 'Fact as the infinite-time limit of reconciliation' as unjustified, citing permanent uncertainty, non-identifiability, and model misspecification as reasons the limit may not exist or may not equal truth even if it does.

sources.note: Step 162's principle that the KnowledgeOS kernel should contain only concepts requiring true system-wide consistency (Identity, Provenance reference, Lineage reference, Authority reference, Integrity, Version, Correlation, TemporalValidity), explicitly excluding Wisdom/Decision/Inquiry/business-specific Action/domain-specific Evidence or Knowledge unless proven otherwise (Kernel != UniversalDomainModel; every kernel addition increases coupling, so the burden of proof for inclusion is high). Pairs this with a 'context projection' idea: an agent receives Projection(H,C) -> Context_C, a task-relevant slice of the full historical lineage H, under the design principle SystemContext ⊇ ActorContext (the actor need not possess the complete history) and a new invariant that context supplied to an actor must be distinguishable from complete historical state, else the actor may wrongly assume it has been given everything that exists. Reinterprets the Gita 'only Krishna knows' insight architecturally as GlobalHistoricalContext (system of record) vs intentionally incomplete LocalActorContext, restated as 'the system preserves the lineage necessary to reconstruct relevant prior states', not 'the system remembers everything' -- and argues a complete-memory-for-every-agent model would be expensive, hard to govern, unsafe, and hard to invalidate/reason about.

Kernel ≠ UniversalDomainModel. ... The kernel should be: small, stable, authoritative. Every concept added to the kernel increases coupling. sources.note: Step 170's central architectural insight: assurance has two directions -- backward traceability answering 'why did this happen?' (Action->Authorization->Decision->Determination->Knowledge->Evidence) and forward learning answering 'what did we learn from what happened?' (Action->Outcome->Observation->Evidence->Knowledge'), combined as Assurance = BackwardTraceability + ForwardLearning. Requires knowledge versioning: superseding knowledge (K^n -> K^{n+1}) must retain the old version where a past decision depended on it (Superseded != Deleted; deleting K^3 after Decision_1 used it would destroy the ability to explain why Decision_1 was reasonable at the time). Distinguishes ValidNow(K) from WasValidAt(K,t) (a claim can be InvalidNow while having been ValidAt(t0)), formalizes decision Justification(D)=<K_v,D_t,Policy_v,Authority,Context> using versions applicable AT DECISION TIME (not today's versions), giving the invariant Decision(D)=>Basis(D,t_D) -- 'temporal justification', stronger than generic auditability -- and a Reconstruct(D) test for whether the epistemic/governance basis of D at t_D can be recovered.

sources.note: A second disciplined philosophical study, run alongside the KR-REP-REDUCTION audit under the same layer-ban and the handoff's own added discipline ('never infer a hierarchy from naming alone'; 'separate empirical results from mathematical claims'). Finds Gita 2.22's garment-changing simile ([EXT], corroboration) frames exactly the preservation-contract question Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(D\S)) -- change of representation, invariance of what the inquiry is about -- while explicitly supplying no way to measure preservation (no counterpart to N_viol, H_hat(Q|R), A_n, F_n); finds 2.16's real/unreal boundary a weak lens only for the audit's adequate/inadequate boundary question, since the audit's own difficulty is that the boundary is contract-relative and possibly non-monotone, which the text does not address; extends the prior study's ground-not-outcome corroboration (G-10) to the audit's adequacy-vs-realization separation (information present vs a specific operator recovering it); and explicitly REFUSES the single most tempting reading -- that 2.50's 'yoga is skill in action' licenses treating representation compactness as a virtue -- naming this 'the 5 digits -> 2 digits trap in Sanskrit dress' and citing the handoff's own section 25 warning that digit count is not a representation-capacity measure. Concludes with zero kernel candidates (fifth consecutive time) and the explicit statement that the study's honest yield is one framing corroboration, one extension, and one refusal, the refusal being the most useful of the three.

sources.note: Step 176 distinguishes four relationships between an actor and a knowledge artifact -- Owns(a,K), CanAccess(a,K), HasInContext(a,K), CanUse(a,K) -- e.g. a human may own a decision while an AI can access but not use it for a given action. Adds a new epistemic dimension, KnowledgeAccess, alongside the existing Identity/Capability/Responsibility/Authority/Accountability five-dimensional model, explicitly not promoted to a sixth governance role but a distinct concern. States Access does not imply Authority as a non-linear lattice (Authority sits above both Capability and Responsibility, which sit above Knowledge, which sits above Access -- though the dimensions are largely orthogonal, not a strict chain), with worked examples: CanRead(AI,Decision_1) does not imply CanChange(AI,Decision_1); CanChange(K) does not imply CanAuthorize(Action); an AI with Access+CodeModification capability can still lack ProductionDeployment authority, while a human release authority can have that authority without code-modification capability -- justifying explicit authorization rather than relying on technical permissions alone.

rows.statement: 20.71-20.73: retrieval can shrink the knowledge gap (Delta_{t+1}⊆Delta_t) or expose previously-invisible missing information, growing it (Delta_{t+1}⊃Delta_t, e.g. discovering 'no sufficiently authoritative source exists'), which is not failure but improved epistemic awareness -- worked example Delta_0=∅ (requirements unknown) -> Delta_1={r1,r2,r3} after rigorous retrieval, giving GapIncrease⇏KnowledgeQualityDecrease, explicitly said to follow from 'the learning theory of Part XVII'; retrieval completeness is contextual -- Complete(R,Q1,Gamma1) does not transfer to Complete(R,Q2,Gamma2), so 'the knowledge base has been completely searched' has no universal meaning without a target/scope/contract.

rows.statement: Requires every KR-ZOOM-OUT-02 estimand to be reported as contract-relative -- never 'what Zoom-out does' unconditionally, only 'what Zoom-out does under this contract, at this standard, in this stratum' -- since P_det is a property of (domain x contract), not of the domain alone (the candidate FR-004 principle); pre-declares, before execution, that if stratum composition moves materially across two epistemic standards this would count as FR-004's seventh convergent instance, explicitly framed as a prediction rather than a post-hoc discovery.
